"""
E1b — Our lead-scoring method against published solutions: same data, same rows, same inputs.

Data: ml/data/Leads.csv (Kaggle "Lead Scoring", X Education: 9,240 real leads, 38.5% converted).

PART A. Four public solutions of the X Education case study, re-run exactly (ml/experiments/published/:
every confusion matrix they printed is reproduced). On EACH solution's own train/test split:
  theirs                    their final logistic regression and their cut-off (their published numbers)
  ours, same inputs         our gradient boosting (the CRM's own configuration, backend/app/ml/training/lead.py, nothing
                            tuned for this file) on the same design matrix their feature selection chose
                            from, trained on the same rows
  ours, new-lead inputs     our gradient boosting on the 9 columns a lead has when it arrives (no column
                            the sales team fills in after contact), same rows
  theirs, no post-contact   their final model refitted without Tags / Lead Quality / Last Activity /
                            Last Notable Activity (what it is worth for a new lead)
  Precise metrics: ROC AUC on the identical test rows with DeLong's 95% interval and DeLong's paired test;
  accuracy at a cut-off chosen on the TRAINING rows by the same rule the solution used (ours: on
  cross-validated training predictions), with McNemar's exact test; log-loss with a paired bootstrap
  interval. Then 30 more random 70/30 splits of the same rows: mean AUC difference with the corrected
  resampled t-interval (Nadeau & Bengio 2003).

PART B. Published numbers whose code is not public, compared under their protocol:
  Mandal, MSc thesis, National College of Ireland (2025): post-contact columns removed, stratified 80/20
  split, random forest: accuracy 79.76%, ROC AUC 0.8605 (threshold chosen on the test set).
  Jadli et al., IJCSE 13(2), 2022: random forest accuracy 93.02%, AUC 0.92 (inputs not listed).
  Yim et al., IJOMFA 5(1), 2024: stacking accuracy 92.33% (inputs not listed in the abstract).

# ── statistics ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def delong(y, *scores):
    """AUCs and their covariance (DeLong et al. 1988; fast algorithm of Sun & Xu 2014)."""
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(bool)
    m, n = int(y.sum()), int((~y).sum())
    S = np.vstack([np.asarray(s, float) for s in scores])
    pos, neg = S[:, y], S[:, ~y]
    tx = np.vstack([rankdata(r) for r in pos])
    ty = np.vstack([rankdata(r) for r in neg])
    tz = np.vstack([rankdata(np.r_[a, b]) for a, b in zip(pos, neg)])
    auc = tz[:, :m].sum(1) / (m * n) - (m + 1) / (2 * n)
    v01 = (tz[:, :m] - tx) / n
    v10 = 1 - (tz[:, m:] - ty) / m
    cov = np.atleast_2d(np.cov(v01)) / m + np.atleast_2d(np.cov(v10)) / n
    return auc, cov


def auc_ci(y, p):
    a, c = delong(y, p)
    se = float(np.sqrt(c[0, 0]))
    return float(a[0]), float(a[0] - 1.96 * se), float(a[0] + 1.96 * se)


def auc_diff(y, p_ours, p_theirs):
    a, c = delong(y, p_ours, p_theirs)
    d = float(a[0] - a[1])
    se = float(np.sqrt(max(c[0, 0] + c[1, 1] - 2 * c[0, 1], 1e-18)))
    p = float(2 * stats.norm.sf(abs(d) / se))
    return {"diff": d, "low": d - 1.96 * se, "high": d + 1.96 * se, "p": p}


def mcnemar(y, pred_ours, pred_theirs):
    ok_o, ok_t = pred_ours == y, pred_theirs == y
    b, c = int(np.sum(ok_o & ~ok_t)), int(np.sum(~ok_o & ok_t))
    p = float(stats.binomtest(min(b, c), b + c, 0.5).pvalue) if b + c else 1.0
    return {"ours_only_right": b, "theirs_only_right": c, "p": p, "diff": float(ok_o.mean() - ok_t.mean())}


def logloss_diff(y, p_ours, p_theirs, seed=0):
    """Paired bootstrap of log-loss(theirs) - log-loss(ours): positive = ours better."""
    y = np.asarray(y, float)
    clip = lambda p: np.clip(np.asarray(p, float), 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
    lo = -(y * np.log(clip(p_ours)) + (1 - y) * np.log(1 - clip(p_ours)))
    lt = -(y * np.log(clip(p_theirs)) + (1 - y) * np.log(1 - clip(p_theirs)))
    d = lt - lo
    pick = np.random.default_rng(seed).integers(0, len(d), (BOOT, len(d)))
    boot = d[pick].mean(1)
    return {
        "diff": float(d.mean()),
        "low": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)),
        "high": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975)),
        "ours": float(lo.mean()),
        "theirs": float(lt.mean()),
    }


def corrected_interval(x, test_share):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    r = len(x)
    se = np.sqrt((1 / r + test_share / (1 - test_share)) * x.var(ddof=1))
    t = stats.t.ppf(0.975, r - 1)
    return float(x.mean()), float(x.mean() - t * se), float(x.mean() + t * se)


def at_cutoff(y, p, cut):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    pred = (np.asarray(p) > cut).astype(int)
    tp, tn = int(np.sum((pred == 1) & (y == 1))), int(np.sum((pred == 0) & (y == 0)))
    fp, fn = int(np.sum((pred == 1) & (y == 0))), int(np.sum((pred == 0) & (y == 1)))
    return {
        "cutoff": float(cut),
        "accuracy": (tp + tn) / len(y),
        "sensitivity": tp / max(tp + fn, 1),
        "specificity": tn / max(tn + fp, 1),
        "precision": tp / max(tp + fp, 1),
        "pred": pred,
    }


def choose_cutoff(y, p, rule):
    """The solutions' own rules: where sensitivity meets specificity, or precision meets recall."""
    grid = np.round(np.arange(0.05, 0.951, 0.01), 2)
    best, gap = 0.5, 9.0
    for c in grid:
        m = at_cutoff(y, p, c)
        g = (
            abs(m["sensitivity"] - m["specificity"])
            if rule == "sensitivity_specificity"
            else abs(m["precision"] - m["sensitivity"])
        )
        if g < gap:
            best, gap = float(c), g
    return best


# ── models ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def ours():
    return clone(T.candidates()["gradient_boosting"])


def fit_predict(make, Xtr, ytr, Xte):
    m = make().fit(Xtr, ytr)
    return m.predict_proba(Xte)[:, 1]


def oof(make, X, y, seed=0):
    """Cross-validated predictions on the training rows (to choose a cut-off without peeking)."""
    y = np.asarray(y)
    out = np.zeros(len(y))
    for tr, te in StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=seed).split(X, y):
        out[te] = fit_predict(
            make, X.iloc[tr] if hasattr(X, "iloc") else X[tr], y[tr], X.iloc[te] if hasattr(X, "iloc") else X[te]
        )
    return out


def mle(Xtr, ytr, Xte):
    m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, solver="newton-cg", max_iter=10000, tol=1e-10)
    m.fit(np.asarray(Xtr, float), np.asarray(ytr))
    return m.predict_proba(np.asarray(Xte, float))[:, 1]


def new_lead_frame():
    rows, y = RL.load_real_leads()
    return F.to_model_frame(rows)[RL.REAL_COLUMNS], y


def new_lead_model():
    return Pipeline([("prep", RL.build_real_preprocessor()), ("clf", ours())])


def is_leaky(col):
    return any(col == s or col.startswith(s + "_") or col.lower().startswith(s.lower() + "_") for s in LEAKY)


# ── part A ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def part_a(frame, y_all, say):
    out = []
    for sol in P.SOLUTIONS:
        t0 = time.time()
        mod = importlib.import_module(f"published.{sol['module']}")
        log = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(log):
            d = mod.reproduce(RL.REAL_DATA)
        rep, rpr = d["reported"]["test"], d["reproduced"]["test"]
        exact = rep["confusion"] == rpr["confusion"]
        Xtr, ytr = d["X_train"].astype(float), d["y_train"].to_numpy().astype(int)
        Xte = d.get("X_test_train_scaled", d["X_test"]).astype(float)
        yte = d["y_test"].to_numpy().astype(int)
        tri, tei = np.asarray(d["train_index"]), np.asarray(d["test_index"])
        assert (y_all[tri] == ytr).all() and (y_all[tei] == yte).all(), "row numbers do not match Leads.csv"
        rule = RULES[sol["key"]]
        theirs = np.asarray(d["test_proba"], float)
        th = at_cutoff(yte, theirs, d["cutoff"])
        # ours on the same inputs
        p_same = fit_predict(ours, Xtr, ytr, Xte)
        c_same = choose_cutoff(ytr, oof(ours, Xtr, ytr), rule)
        # ours on the inputs a new lead has
        Ftr, Fte = frame.iloc[tri], frame.iloc[tei]
        p_new = fit_predict(new_lead_model, Ftr, ytr, Fte)
        c_new = choose_cutoff(ytr, oof(new_lead_model, Ftr, ytr), rule)
        # their model without the post-contact columns
        clean = [f for f in d["final_features"] if f not in d["leaky_final_features"] and not is_leaky(f)]
        p_clean = mle(Xtr[clean], ytr, Xte[clean]) if clean else np.full(len(yte), ytr.mean())
        c_clean = choose_cutoff(ytr, mle(Xtr[clean], ytr, Xtr[clean]) if clean else np.full(len(ytr), ytr.mean()), rule)
        res = {
            "key": sol["key"],
            "label": sol["label"],
            "url": sol["url"],
            "commit": sol["commit"],
            "reproduced_exactly": bool(exact),
            "n_train": int(len(ytr)),
            "n_test": int(len(yte)),
            "test_converted": float(yte.mean()),
            "design_columns": int(Xtr.shape[1]),
            "final_features": d["final_features"],
            "leaky_final_features": d["leaky_final_features"],
            "leaky_columns_in_design": d["leaky_columns_in_design"],
            "rule": rule,
            "reported": {k: rep.get(k) for k in ("accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity", "precision", "roc_auc")},
            "notes": d.get("notes", ""),
        }
        models = {
            "theirs": (theirs, d["cutoff"]),
            "ours_same_inputs": (p_same, c_same),
            "ours_new_lead_inputs": (p_new, c_new),
            "theirs_no_post_contact": (p_clean, c_clean),
        }
        res["models"] = {}
        for name, (p, cut) in models.items():
            m = at_cutoff(yte, p, cut)
            a, lo, hi = auc_ci(yte, p)
            res["models"][name] = {
                "auc": a,
                "auc_low": lo,
                "auc_high": hi,
                "log_loss": float(log_loss(yte, np.clip(p, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))),
                **{k: v for k, v in m.items() if k != "pred"},
            }
        res["vs_theirs"] = {}
        for name in ("ours_same_inputs", "ours_new_lead_inputs"):
            p, cut = models[name]
            res["vs_theirs"][name] = {
                "auc": auc_diff(yte, p, theirs),
                "accuracy": mcnemar(yte, at_cutoff(yte, p, cut)["pred"], th["pred"]),
                "log_loss": logloss_diff(yte, p, theirs),
            }
        # 30 more random splits of the same rows (their style: 70/30, not stratified)
        D = pd.concat([Xtr, Xte]).astype(float)
        Dy = np.r_[ytr, yte]
        Fall = pd.concat([Ftr, Fte])
        diffs_same, diffs_new, auc_t, auc_s, auc_n = [], [], [], [], []
        for r in range(REPEAT_SPLITS):
            a_idx, b_idx = train_test_split(np.arange(len(Dy)), train_size=0.7, random_state=1000 + r)
            pt = mle(D.iloc[a_idx][d["final_features"]], Dy[a_idx], D.iloc[b_idx][d["final_features"]])
            ps = fit_predict(ours, D.iloc[a_idx], Dy[a_idx], D.iloc[b_idx])
            pn = fit_predict(new_lead_model, Fall.iloc[a_idx], Dy[a_idx], Fall.iloc[b_idx])
            at, as_, an = (roc_auc_score(Dy[b_idx], q) for q in (pt, ps, pn))
            auc_t.append(at), auc_s.append(as_), auc_n.append(an)
            diffs_same.append(as_ - at), diffs_new.append(an - at)
        res["repeated_splits"] = {
            "splits": REPEAT_SPLITS,
            "theirs_auc": corrected_interval(auc_t, 0.3),
            "ours_same_inputs_auc": corrected_interval(auc_s, 0.3),
            "ours_new_lead_inputs_auc": corrected_interval(auc_n, 0.3),
            "ours_same_minus_theirs": corrected_interval(diffs_same, 0.3),
            "ours_new_minus_theirs": corrected_interval(diffs_new, 0.3),
            "ours_same_wins": int(np.sum(np.array(diffs_same) > 0)),
            "ours_new_wins": int(np.sum(np.array(diffs_new) > 0)),
        }
        out.append(res)
        say(
            f"  {sol['label']}: reproduced exactly: {exact}; AUC theirs {res['models']['theirs']['auc']:.4f}, "
            f"ours same inputs {res['models']['ours_same_inputs']['auc']:.4f}, ours new-lead inputs "
            f"{res['models']['ours_new_lead_inputs']['auc']:.4f} ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)"
        )
    return out


# ── part B ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def part_b(frame, y, say):
    """Mandal's protocol (stratified 80/20, no post-contact column) with our 9 new-lead columns."""
    aucs, accs, cuts = [], [], []
    t0 = time.time()
    for r in range(MANDAL_SPLITS):
        tr, te = train_test_split(np.arange(len(y)), test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=r)
        p = fit_predict(new_lead_model, frame.iloc[tr], y[tr], frame.iloc[te])
        q = oof(new_lead_model, frame.iloc[tr], y[tr], seed=r)
        grid = np.round(np.arange(0.30, 0.701, 0.01), 2)  # Mandal's grid, but searched on TRAINING rows
        cut = float(grid[np.argmax([((q > c).astype(int) == y[tr]).mean() for c in grid])])
        aucs.append(roc_auc_score(y[te], p))
        accs.append(((p > cut).astype(int) == y[te]).mean())
        cuts.append(cut)
    say(f"  Mandal protocol: {MANDAL_SPLITS} splits ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)")
    aucs, accs = np.array(aucs), np.array(accs)
    return {
        "splits": MANDAL_SPLITS,
        "auc_mean": float(aucs.mean()),
        "auc_p2_5": float(np.quantile(aucs, 0.025)),
        "auc_p97_5": float(np.quantile(aucs, 0.975)),
        "auc_interval": corrected_interval(aucs, 0.2),
        "share_auc_above_published": float(np.mean(aucs > 0.8605)),
        "accuracy_mean": float(accs.mean()),
        "accuracy_interval": corrected_interval(accs, 0.2),
        "share_accuracy_above_published": float(np.mean(accs > 0.7976)),
        "cutoff_mean": float(np.mean(cuts)),
    }


def leaky_ceiling(y, say):
    """Our gradient boosting WITH the post-contact columns, 5-fold cross-validation (contrast only)."""
    d = pd.read_csv(RL.REAL_DATA)
    base, _ = new_lead_frame()
    X = base.copy()
    for c in LEAKY:
        X[c] = d[c].astype(str)
    from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
    from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder

    prep = ColumnTransformer(
        [
            ("base", RL.build_real_preprocessor(), RL.REAL_COLUMNS),
            ("leak", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False), LEAKY),
        ]
    )
    p = oof(lambda: Pipeline([("prep", prep), ("clf", ours())]), X, y, seed=42)
    cut = 0.5
    return {"auc": auc_ci(y, p), "accuracy": float(((p > cut).astype(int) == y).mean())}


# ── report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def pct(x):
    return "—" if x is None else f"{100 * x:.1f}%"


def ci(a, lo, hi, d=3):
    return f"{a:.{d}f} [{lo:.{d}f}, {hi:.{d}f}]"


def pval(p):
    return "< 0.0001" if p < 1e-4 else f"{p:.4f}"


def wins_text(reps):
    lo, hi = min(x["ours_same_wins"] for x in reps), max(x["ours_same_wins"] for x in reps)
    return f"{lo}" if lo == hi else f"{lo}–{hi}"


def report(A, B, leak, y):
    short = lambda r: r["label"].split(" / ")[0]
    rs = {r["key"]: r for r in A}
    same = [r["vs_theirs"]["ours_same_inputs"]["auc"] for r in A]
    reps = [r["repeated_splits"] for r in A]
    leaky = [r for r in A if r["leaky_final_features"]]
    new_aucs = [r["models"]["ours_new_lead_inputs"]["auc"] for r in A]
    leakfree_acc = max(
        [r["models"]["ours_new_lead_inputs"]["accuracy"] for r in A]
        + [r["models"]["theirs_no_post_contact"]["accuracy"] for r in A]
        + [B["accuracy_mean"]]
    )
    best_leaky_auc = max(r["models"]["theirs"]["auc"] for r in leaky)
    best_leaky_acc = max(
        [r["models"]["theirs"]["accuracy"] for r in leaky]
        + [pb["accuracy"] for pb in PUBLISHED_B if not pb["who"].startswith("Mandal")]
    )
    L = [
        "# E1b Our lead scoring vs published solutions (X Education, 9,240 real leads)",
        "",
        "Same data (byte-identical Leads.csv), same rows, same inputs. The precise metric is ROC AUC on the identical "
        "test rows with DeLong's 95% interval and paired test, repeated on 30 new splits with the corrected resampled "
        "t-interval; accuracy is compared at a cut-off chosen on the training rows by each solution's own rule "
        "(McNemar's exact test).",
        "",
        "**Post-contact columns** (Tags, Lead Quality, Lead Profile, Last Activity, Last Notable Activity, Asymmetrique "
        "scores) are filled in by the sales team after contacting a lead, so a new lead never has them: a model that "
        "uses them cannot score new leads.",
        "",
        "## The records, in one table",
        "",
        "| Comparison | Best earlier result (published, or their model re-run) | Ours | How it is measured |",
        "|---|---|---|---|",
        f"| Same rows and same inputs as each of {len(A)} public solutions | AUC "
        f"{min(r['models']['theirs']['auc'] for r in A):.3f}–{max(r['models']['theirs']['auc'] for r in A):.3f} | higher by "
        f"{min(x['diff'] for x in same):+.3f} to {max(x['diff'] for x in same):+.3f} on their split; better in "
        f"{wins_text(reps)} of {REPEAT_SPLITS} new splits for each"
        f"{' (every 95% interval above zero)' if all(x['ours_same_minus_theirs'][1] > 0 for x in reps) else ''} | DeLong on the "
        f"identical test rows; {REPEAT_SPLITS} new 70/30 splits |",
        f"| Only inputs a new lead has | AUC 0.8605 (Mandal 2025, stratified 80/20); "
        f"{rs['lohani']['models']['theirs']['auc']:.3f} (Lohani & Bansal, on its split) | AUC {B['auc_mean']:.3f} on "
        f"{B['splits']} stratified 80/20 splits (above 0.8605 in {100 * B['share_auc_above_published']:.0f}%); "
        f"{rs['lohani']['models']['ours_new_lead_inputs']['auc']:.3f} on Lohani & Bansal's split — with 9 columns | "
        "their protocol |",
        f"| With post-contact columns (not valid for new leads) | AUC {best_leaky_auc:.3f}, accuracy "
        f"{pct(best_leaky_acc)} | AUC {leak['auc'][0]:.3f} [{leak['auc'][1]:.3f}, {leak['auc'][2]:.3f}], accuracy "
        f"{pct(leak['accuracy'])} | 5-fold cross-validation |",
        "",
        "## A. Four public solutions, re-run exactly, on their own splits",
        "",
        "| Public solution | Post-contact columns in its model | Test rows | Their AUC | Ours, same inputs | "
        "Ours − theirs (DeLong p) | Ours, new-lead inputs only | Their model without post-contact columns |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in A:
        m, v = r["models"], r["vs_theirs"]["ours_same_inputs"]["auc"]
        lk = (
            f"{len(r['leaky_final_features'])} of {len(r['final_features'])}"
            if r["leaky_final_features"]
            else f"none (0 of {len(r['final_features'])})"
        )
        L.append(
            f"| [{r['label']}]({r['url']}) | {lk} | {r['n_test']:,} | {ci(m['theirs']['auc'], m['theirs']['auc_low'], m['theirs']['auc_high'])} | "
            f"{ci(m['ours_same_inputs']['auc'], m['ours_same_inputs']['auc_low'], m['ours_same_inputs']['auc_high'])} | "
            f"{v['diff']:+.3f} [{v['low']:+.3f}, {v['high']:+.3f}] (p {pval(v['p'])}) | "
            f"{ci(m['ours_new_lead_inputs']['auc'], m['ours_new_lead_inputs']['auc_low'], m['ours_new_lead_inputs']['auc_high'])} | "
            f"{m['theirs_no_post_contact']['auc']:.3f} |"
        )
    L += [
        "",
        "Every confusion matrix the notebooks printed was reproduced exactly: "
        + ", ".join(f"{short(r)} {'yes' if r['reproduced_exactly'] else 'NO'}" for r in A)
        + ". Sivagiri12's cleaning turns every lead from the API into a missing value, so its rows are the 5,496 leads "
        "that did not come from the API.",
        "",
    ]
    L += [
        "### Accuracy, sensitivity and specificity at each solution's own cut-off rule",
        "",
        "| Public solution | Model | Cut-off | Accuracy | Sensitivity | Specificity | Precision | Log-loss |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    names = {
        "theirs": "theirs (published)",
        "ours_same_inputs": "ours, same inputs",
        "ours_new_lead_inputs": "ours, new-lead inputs",
        "theirs_no_post_contact": "theirs without post-contact columns",
    }
    for r in A:
        for k, nm in names.items():
            m = r["models"][k]
            L.append(
                f"| {short(r)} | {nm} | {m['cutoff']:.2f} | {pct(m['accuracy'])} | {pct(m['sensitivity'])} | "
                f"{pct(m['specificity'])} | {pct(m['precision'])} | {m['log_loss']:.4f} |"
            )
    L += [
        "",
        "| Public solution | Ours (same inputs) vs theirs: accuracy | McNemar p | Log-loss lower by [95% CI] |",
        "|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in A:
        v = r["vs_theirs"]["ours_same_inputs"]
        L.append(
            f"| {short(r)} | {100 * v['accuracy']['diff']:+.1f} points ({v['accuracy']['ours_only_right']} "
            f"leads only ours got right, {v['accuracy']['theirs_only_right']} only theirs) | {pval(v['accuracy']['p'])} | "
            f"{v['log_loss']['diff']:+.4f} [{v['log_loss']['low']:+.4f}, {v['log_loss']['high']:+.4f}] |"
        )
    L += [
        "",
        f"### {REPEAT_SPLITS} more random 70/30 splits of each solution's rows",
        "",
        "Mean AUC with the corrected resampled t-interval (Nadeau & Bengio 2003); their model keeps its published "
        "feature list (chosen on the original split, which can only favour it).",
        "",
        "| Public solution | Their AUC | Ours, same inputs | Ours − theirs | Ours better in | Ours, new-lead inputs | "
        "New-lead − theirs |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in A:
        s = r["repeated_splits"]
        L.append(
            f"| {short(r)} | {ci(*s['theirs_auc'])} | {ci(*s['ours_same_inputs_auc'])} | "
            f"{s['ours_same_minus_theirs'][0]:+.3f} [{s['ours_same_minus_theirs'][1]:+.3f}, {s['ours_same_minus_theirs'][2]:+.3f}] | "
            f"{s['ours_same_wins']} of {s['splits']} | {ci(*s['ours_new_lead_inputs_auc'])} | "
            f"{s['ours_new_minus_theirs'][0]:+.3f} [{s['ours_new_minus_theirs'][1]:+.3f}, {s['ours_new_minus_theirs'][2]:+.3f}] |"
        )
    L += [
        "",
        "## B. Published results whose code is not public",
        "",
        "| Publication | Post-contact columns | Their protocol | Their result | Ours |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for pb in PUBLISHED_B:
        theirs_txt = f"{pb['model']}: accuracy {pct(pb['accuracy'])}" + (f", AUC {pb['auc']:.4g}" if pb["auc"] else "")
        if pb["note"]:
            theirs_txt += f" ({pb['note']})"
        if pb["who"].startswith("Mandal"):
            o = (
                f"same protocol, 9 new-lead columns, {B['splits']} stratified 80/20 splits: AUC {B['auc_mean']:.3f} (95% of "
                f"splits {B['auc_p2_5']:.3f}–{B['auc_p97_5']:.3f}; above {pb['auc']} in "
                f"{100 * B['share_auc_above_published']:.0f}%), accuracy {pct(B['accuracy_mean'])} with the cut-off chosen "
                "on the training rows"
            )
        else:
            o = (
                f"with post-contact columns (5-fold CV): AUC {leak['auc'][0]:.3f}, accuracy {pct(leak['accuracy'])}. "
                f"Without them the best accuracy in this study is {pct(leakfree_acc)}: above 90% needs post-contact columns"
            )
        L.append(f"| [{pb['who']}]({pb['url']}) | {pb['post_contact']} | {pb['protocol']} | {theirs_txt} | {o} |")
    better = [x for x in same if x["diff"] > 0 and x["p"] < 0.05]
    worse = [x for x in same if x["diff"] < 0 and x["p"] < 0.05]
    lo = rs["lohani"]["vs_theirs"]["ours_new_lead_inputs"]["auc"]
    lo_rep = rs["lohani"]["repeated_splits"]
    L += [
        "",
        "## What this shows (computed from the numbers above)",
        "",
        f"- **Same rows, same inputs:** on each solution's own split our AUC is higher for all {len(A)} "
        f"({len(better)} significantly, DeLong p < 0.05; {len(A) - len(better) - len(worse)} not significantly; "
        f"{len(worse)} lower), and on {REPEAT_SPLITS} new splits ours is better in "
        f"{', '.join(str(x['ours_same_wins']) for x in reps)} of {REPEAT_SPLITS} with every interval above zero"
        f"{'' if all(x['ours_same_minus_theirs'][1] > 0 for x in reps) else ' (NOT for all)'}. Nothing was tuned on "
        "their data: the gradient boosting is the CRM's own configuration.",
        "- **Their high numbers come from post-contact columns.** Refitted without those columns, each solution's own "
        "model falls: "
        + "; ".join(
            f"{short(r)} AUC {r['models']['theirs']['auc']:.3f} → "
            f"{r['models']['theirs_no_post_contact']['auc']:.3f}"
            for r in leaky
        )
        + ".",
        f"- **On what a new lead has**, our 9-column model scores AUC {min(new_aucs):.3f}–{max(new_aucs):.3f} on the four "
        f"splits; against the only leak-free public solution (Lohani & Bansal) on its own rows: "
        f"{lo['diff']:+.3f} [{lo['low']:+.3f}, {lo['high']:+.3f}] (DeLong p {pval(lo['p'])}), and "
        f"{lo_rep['ours_new_minus_theirs'][0]:+.3f} [{lo_rep['ours_new_minus_theirs'][1]:+.3f}, "
        f"{lo_rep['ours_new_minus_theirs'][2]:+.3f}] over {REPEAT_SPLITS} new splits (better in {lo_rep['ours_new_wins']}). "
        f"Under the leak-free thesis's protocol it reaches AUC {B['auc_mean']:.3f} on average "
        f"({100 * B['share_auc_above_published']:.0f}% of {B['splits']} splits above the thesis's 0.8605).",
        f"- **The honest ceiling.** Without post-contact columns no model in this study goes beyond AUC "
        f"{max(new_aucs + [B['auc_p97_5']]):.3f} or accuracy {pct(leakfree_acc)}. The accuracies above 90% reported "
        "for this file (two of the public solutions, which use post-contact columns; Jadli et al.; Yim et al., whose "
        "inputs are not listed) are out of reach for a model that scores new leads.",
        f"- Leads in the file: {len(y):,}; converted {100 * y.mean():.1f}%.",
    ]
    return L


def main():
    t0 = time.time()
    say = lambda s: print(s, flush=True)
    frame, y = new_lead_frame()
    if "--report-only" in sys.argv:  # rewrite the .md from the saved .json
        with open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "published_benchmark.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            saved = json.load(f)
        lines = report(saved["part_a"], saved["part_b_mandal_protocol"], saved["with_post_contact_columns"], y)
        with open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "published_benchmark.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        print("\n".join(lines))
        return
    A = part_a(frame, y, say)
    B = part_b(frame, y, say)
    leak = leaky_ceiling(y, say)
    lines = report(A, B, leak, y)
    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "published_benchmark.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    with open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "published_benchmark.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(
            {"part_a": A, "part_b_mandal_protocol": B, "with_post_contact_columns": leak, "published_b": PUBLISHED_B},
            f,
            indent=1,
            default=float,
        )
    print("\n" + "\n".join(lines))
    print(f"\n({time.time() - t0:.0f} s) Saved ml/results/published_benchmark.md")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Helpers for the experiments that run whole simulated histories: each history runs in its own temporary copy
of the project (code, crm_settings.json and the starting models), so your own database and models are never
touched, and an experiment can change a setting in its copy only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
SKIP = shutil.ignore_patterns(
    "venv",
    ".venv",
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    ".git",
    "__pycache__",
    "*.db",
    "*.db-wal",
    "*.db-shm",
    "*.db-journal",
    "*.previous.pkl",
    "logs",
    "frontend",
    "docs",
    "results",
    "xeducation-update-*",
    "xeducation-backup-*",
)
STARTERS = ("lead_model.starter.pkl", "nba_model.starter.pkl")


def model_dir() -> str:
    """Where this project keeps its trained models (backend/data/models, or DATA_DIR/models)."""
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "backend"))
    from app.core.config import get_settings

    return str(get_settings().model_dir)


def require_starting_models() -> None:
    for name in STARTERS:
        if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(model_dir(), name)):
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} not found in {model_dir()}: run 'python -m app.cli bootstrap' in backend first.")


def copy_project(dest: str) -> str:
    """A copy of the project for one history, with this project's starting models."""
    shutil.copytree(ROOT, dest, ignore=SKIP)
    models = os.path.join(dest, "backend", "data", "models")
    os.makedirs(models, exist_ok=True)
    src = model_dir()
    for name in os.listdir(src):
        if name.endswith((".pkl", ".json")):
            shutil.copy2(os.path.join(src, name), os.path.join(models, name))
    return dest


def env_for(dest: str) -> dict:
    """Environment of a process working on a copy: its own data folder, no email, no Gemini, no live learners."""
    return dict(
        os.environ,
        PYTHONUTF8="1",
        OMP_NUM_THREADS="1",
        DATA_DIR=os.path.join(dest, "backend", "data"),
        GEMINI_API_KEY="",
        GMAIL_USER="",
        GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD="",
        SIMULATION_ENABLED="false",
        PYTHONPATH=os.path.join(dest, "backend"),
    )


def run_history(dest: str, n: int, days: int, seed: int, quiet: bool = True) -> None:
    """python -m app.cli history create in the copy (its own code, settings and data)."""
    subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "app.cli", "history", "create", "--n", str(n), "--days", str(days), "--seed", str(seed)],
        cwd=os.path.join(dest, "backend"),
        env=env_for(dest),
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL if quiet else None,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE if quiet else None,
    )


def use_copy(folder: str):
    """Inside an analysis process: import the copy's own code (or this project's, for a folder kept without code)
    and point it at the copy's database. Returns app.db."""
    code = folder if os.path.exists(os.path.join(folder, "backend", "app")) else ROOT
    os.environ["DATA_DIR"] = os.path.join(folder, "backend", "data")
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(code, "backend"))
    os.chdir(os.path.join(folder, "backend"))
    from app import db

    db.DB_PATH = os.path.join(folder, "backend", "data", "xeducation.db")
    return db

"""Faithful re-implementation of Lead_Scoring_Case_Study,

usage: python ml/experiments/published/lohani.py <path to Leads.csv> [<output .pkl path>]

def metrics_at(y, p, cutoff):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    pred = (p > cutoff).astype(int)  # notebooks: 1 if x > cutoff else 0
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    n = len(y)
    return {"cutoff": float(cutoff), "n": int(n),
            "confusion": [[int(tn), int(fp)], [int(fn), int(tp)]],
            "accuracy": (tp + tn) / n, "sensitivity": tp / (tp + fn),
            "specificity": tn / (tn + fp), "precision": tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else float("nan"),
            "npv": tn / (tn + fn) if tn + fn else float("nan"), "fpr": fp / (tn + fp),
            "f1": 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), "roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, p))}


def run_rfe(X, y, reported_ranking, n_select, notes):
    """RFE(LogisticRegression(), n) as in the notebook, run two ways.

    The installed scikit-learn (1.6.1) minimises the MEAN log-loss with lbfgs and stops at
    gtol=tol, while the older versions the notebooks ran minimised C * SUM(log-loss) + penalty, so
    the same default tol=1e-4 stopped much later. LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / n_samples) reproduces the old stopping rule; the literal
    1.6.1 defaults are run as well and reported."""
    out = {}
    for key, est in (("old_sklearn_emulation", LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / len(X))),
                     ("sklearn_1_6_defaults", LogisticRegression())):
        r = RFE(est, n_features_to_select=n_select).fit(X, y)
        sel = list(X.columns[r.support_])
        rep_sel = [c for c in X.columns if reported_ranking[c] == 1]
        same = int(sum(reported_ranking[c] == k for c, k in zip(X.columns, r.ranking_)))
        out[key] = {"selected": sel, "selection_matches_notebook": set(sel) == set(rep_sel),
                    "identical_ranks": f"{same}/{X.shape[1]}",
                    "only_reproduced": sorted(set(sel) - set(rep_sel)),
                    "only_notebook": sorted(set(rep_sel) - set(sel))}
        print(f"RFE({n_select}) {key:22s}: selection == notebook: {set(sel) == set(rep_sel)}; "
              f"identical ranks {same}/{X.shape[1]}"
              + ("" if set(sel) == set(rep_sel) else
                 f"; only reproduced {out[key]['only_reproduced']}, only notebook {out[key]['only_notebook']}"))
    e, d = out["old_sklearn_emulation"], out["sklearn_1_6_defaults"]
    notes.append(f"RFE: old-sklearn emulation (tol=1e-4/n) matches the notebook's printed selection: "
                 f"{e['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks {e['identical_ranks']}); literal "
                 f"sklearn 1.6.1 defaults: {d['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks "
                 f"{d['identical_ranks']}, only reproduced {d['only_reproduced']}, only notebook "
                 f"{d['only_notebook']}). The final model uses the notebook's final feature list either way.")
    return out


def fit_mle(X, y):
    """Unpenalised logistic regression with intercept == statsmodels GLM(Binomial) MLE."""
    m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, solver="newton-cg", max_iter=10000, tol=1e-10)
    m.fit(X.astype(float).values, np.asarray(y))
    return m


def show(rep, rpr, keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity", "precision", "f1", "roc_auc")):
    for k in keys:
        a, b = rep.get(k), rpr.get(k)
        a_s = "   n/a  " if a is None else f"{a:.6f}"
        d = "" if a is None else f"  diff {100 * (b - a):+.3f} pp"
        print(f"    {k:12s} reported {a_s}  reproduced {b:.6f}{d}")
    print(f"    confusion    reported {rep.get('confusion')}  reproduced {rpr['confusion']}")

          f" precision {ts['precision']:.6f} auc {ts['roc_auc']:.6f} confusion {ts['confusion']}")

    design_cols = list(X_train.columns)

    leaky_final = [c for c in FINAL_FEATURES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for s in LEAKY_SOURCES)]
    notes.append(
        "Rows: 9,240 -> 9,103 (rows with missing TotalVisits/Page Views dropped). Columns with "
        ">=35% missing dropped (Specialization, How did you hear, Tags, Lead Quality, Lead Profile, "

        "split. 'Lead Source_Olark Chat' and 'Lead Origin_Landing Page Submission' dropped by hand "

        "is printed; train AUC 0.86 appears only in markdown.")
    out = {"name": NAME, "repo": REPO,
           "X_train": X_train, "X_test": X_test, "X_test_train_scaled": X_test_train_scaled,
           "y_train": y_train, "y_test": y_test,
           "train_index": np.asarray(X_train.index), "test_index": np.asarray(X_test.index),
           "final_features": FINAL_FEATURES, "cutoff": CUTOFF,
           "test_proba": test_proba, "train_proba": train_proba,
           "reported": REPORTED, "reproduced": reproduced,
           "leaky_final_features": leaky_final, "leaky_columns_in_design": leaky_in_design,
           "notes": " ".join(notes)}
    if out_path:
        with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(out, f)
    print("leaky final features:", leaky_final)
    print("leaky source columns in design matrix:", leaky_in_design)
    print("design matrix:", X_train.shape, X_test.shape, "->", out_path)
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: python ml/experiments/published/lohani.py <Leads.csv> [<out.pkl>]")
    reproduce(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)

def metrics_at(y, p, cutoff):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    pred = (p > cutoff).astype(int)  # notebooks: 1 if x > cutoff else 0
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    n = len(y)
    return {"cutoff": float(cutoff), "n": int(n),
            "confusion": [[int(tn), int(fp)], [int(fn), int(tp)]],
            "accuracy": (tp + tn) / n, "sensitivity": tp / (tp + fn),
            "specificity": tn / (tn + fp), "precision": tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else float("nan"),
            "npv": tn / (tn + fn) if tn + fn else float("nan"), "fpr": fp / (tn + fp),
            "f1": 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), "roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, p))}


def run_rfe(X, y, reported_ranking, n_select, notes):
    """RFE(LogisticRegression(), n) as in the notebook, run two ways.

    The installed scikit-learn (1.6.1) minimises the MEAN log-loss with lbfgs and stops at
    gtol=tol, while the older versions the notebooks ran minimised C * SUM(log-loss) + penalty, so
    the same default tol=1e-4 stopped much later. LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / n_samples) reproduces the old stopping rule; the literal
    1.6.1 defaults are run as well and reported."""
    out = {}
    for key, est in (("old_sklearn_emulation", LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / len(X))),
                     ("sklearn_1_6_defaults", LogisticRegression())):
        r = RFE(est, n_features_to_select=n_select).fit(X, y)
        sel = list(X.columns[r.support_])
        rep_sel = [c for c in X.columns if reported_ranking[c] == 1]
        same = int(sum(reported_ranking[c] == k for c, k in zip(X.columns, r.ranking_)))
        out[key] = {"selected": sel, "selection_matches_notebook": set(sel) == set(rep_sel),
                    "identical_ranks": f"{same}/{X.shape[1]}",
                    "only_reproduced": sorted(set(sel) - set(rep_sel)),
                    "only_notebook": sorted(set(rep_sel) - set(sel))}
        print(f"RFE({n_select}) {key:22s}: selection == notebook: {set(sel) == set(rep_sel)}; "
              f"identical ranks {same}/{X.shape[1]}"
              + ("" if set(sel) == set(rep_sel) else
                 f"; only reproduced {out[key]['only_reproduced']}, only notebook {out[key]['only_notebook']}"))
    e, d = out["old_sklearn_emulation"], out["sklearn_1_6_defaults"]
    notes.append(f"RFE: old-sklearn emulation (tol=1e-4/n) matches the notebook's printed selection: "
                 f"{e['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks {e['identical_ranks']}); literal "
                 f"sklearn 1.6.1 defaults: {d['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks "
                 f"{d['identical_ranks']}, only reproduced {d['only_reproduced']}, only notebook "
                 f"{d['only_notebook']}). The final model uses the notebook's final feature list either way.")
    return out


def fit_mle(X, y):
    """Unpenalised logistic regression with intercept == statsmodels GLM(Binomial) MLE."""
    m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, solver="newton-cg", max_iter=10000, tol=1e-10)
    m.fit(X.astype(float).values, np.asarray(y))
    return m


def show(rep, rpr, keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity", "precision", "f1", "roc_auc")):
    for k in keys:
        a, b = rep.get(k), rpr.get(k)
        a_s = "   n/a  " if a is None else f"{a:.6f}"
        d = "" if a is None else f"  diff {100 * (b - a):+.3f} pp"
        print(f"    {k:12s} reported {a_s}  reproduced {b:.6f}{d}")
    print(f"    confusion    reported {rep.get('confusion')}  reproduced {rpr['confusion']}")


def reproduce(csv_path, out_path=None):
    """Re-run the notebook on csv_path; returns the dict described in published/__init__.py."""
    notes = []
    lead_df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)                                            # [6]
    assert lead_df.shape == (9240, 37)

    # ---- Step 2: data cleaning
    lead_df = lead_df.drop(["Lead Number", "Prospect ID"], axis=1)            # [14]
    lead_df = lead_df.replace("Select", np.nan)                                 # [16]
    pct = round(100 * (lead_df.isnull().sum() / len(lead_df.index)), 2)
    lead_df = lead_df.drop(lead_df.loc[:, list(pct > 52)].columns, axis=1)    # [19]
    assert "Lead Profile" not in lead_df and "How did you hear about X Education" not in lead_df
    assert "Lead Quality" in lead_df                                            # 51.59% kept
    lead_df["Lead Quality"] = lead_df["Lead Quality"].replace(np.nan, "Not Sure")  # [25]
    asym_list = ["Asymmetrique Activity Index", "Asymmetrique Profile Index",
                 "Asymmetrique Activity Score", "Asymmetrique Profile Score"]
    lead_df = lead_df.drop(asym_list, axis=1)                                   # [29]
    lead_df["City"] = lead_df["City"].replace(np.nan, "Mumbai")                 # [33]
    lead_df["Specialization"] = lead_df["Specialization"].replace(np.nan, "Others")  # [36]
    for var in ["Tags", "What matters most to you in choosing a course",
                "What is your current occupation", "Country"]:                  # [37] [39]
        top_frequent = lead_df[var].describe()["top"]
        lead_df[var] = lead_df[var].replace(np.nan, top_frequent)
    lead_df.dropna(inplace=True)                                                # [45]
    assert len(lead_df) == 9074                                                 # [54] count 9074

    # ---- outlier capping at the 95th percentile                                 [57]
    for var in ["TotalVisits", "Page Views Per Visit"]:
        percentile = lead_df[var].quantile([0.95]).values
        lead_df.loc[lead_df[var] >= percentile[0], var] = percentile[0]   # notebook used chained assignment
    assert lead_df["TotalVisits"].max() == 10.0                                 # [105] max 10

    # ---- category merging
    lead_df["Lead Source"] = lead_df["Lead Source"].replace(["google"], "Google")  # [69]
    categories = lead_df["Lead Source"].unique()                                # [70]
    assert list(categories) == ["Olark Chat", "Organic Search", "Direct Traffic", "Google",
                                "Referral Sites", "Reference", "Welingak Website", "Facebook",
                                "blog", "Pay per Click Ads", "bing", "Social Media", "WeLearn",
                                "Click2call", "Live Chat", "welearnblog_Home", "youtubechannel",
                                "testone", "Press_Release", "NC_EDM"]
    lead_df["Lead Source"] = lead_df["Lead Source"].replace(list(categories[8:]), "Others")  # [71]
    categories = lead_df["Last Activity"].unique()                              # [77]
    assert list(categories[-5:]) == ["Visited Booth in Tradeshow", "Approached upfront",
                                     "Resubscribed to emails", "Email Received", "Email Marked Spam"]
    lead_df["Last Activity"] = lead_df["Last Activity"].replace(list(categories[-5:]), "Others")  # [79]
    categories = lead_df["Tags"].unique()                                       # [91]
    assert list(categories[-8:]) == ["Still Thinking", "Lost to Others",
                                     "Shall take in the next coming month", "Lateral student",
                                     "Interested in Next batch", "Recognition issue (DEC approval)",
                                     "Want to take admission but has financial problems",
                                     "University not recognized"]
    lead_df["Tags"] = lead_df["Tags"].replace(list(categories[-8:]), "Others")  # [93]
    categories = lead_df["Last Notable Activity"].unique()                      # [97]
    assert list(categories[-6:]) == ["Approached upfront", "Resubscribed to emails",
                                     "View in browser link Clicked", "Form Submitted on Website",
                                     "Email Received", "Email Marked Spam"]
    lead_df["Last Notable Activity"] = lead_df["Last Notable Activity"].replace(
        list(categories[-6:]), "Others")                                        # [99]
    lead_df = lead_df.drop(["Do Not Call", "Country", "What matters most to you in choosing a course",
                            "Search", "Magazine", "Newspaper Article", "X Education Forums",
                            "Newspaper", "Digital Advertisement", "Through Recommendations",
                            "Receive More Updates About Our Courses",
                            "Update me on Supply Chain Content", "Get updates on DM Content",
                            "I agree to pay the amount through cheque",
                            "A free copy of Mastering The Interview"], axis=1)   # [102]
    assert lead_df.shape == (9074, 14)                                          # [104]

    # ---- Step 4: data preparation
    lead_df["Do Not Email"] = lead_df["Do Not Email"].map({"Yes": 1, "No": 0})  # [107]
    cat_var = list(lead_df.columns[lead_df.dtypes == "object"])                 # [110]
    assert cat_var == ["Lead Origin", "Lead Source", "Last Activity", "Specialization",
                       "What is your current occupation", "Tags", "Lead Quality", "City",
                       "Last Notable Activity"]
    dummy = pd.get_dummies(lead_df[cat_var], drop_first=True).astype("uint8")   # [111] (uint8 as in pandas<2)
    lead_df = pd.concat([lead_df, dummy], axis=1)
    lead_df = lead_df.drop(cat_var, axis=1)
    assert lead_df.shape == (9074, 88)                                          # [112] 88 columns

    X = lead_df.drop(["Converted"], axis=1)                                     # [115]
    y = lead_df["Converted"]
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, train_size=0.7, test_size=0.3, random_state=100)                  # [116]
    assert list(X_train.index[:5]) == SPLIT_HEAD["train"]                       # [121] head
    assert list(X_test.index[:5]) == SPLIT_HEAD["test"]                         # [193] head

    num_var = ["TotalVisits", "Total Time Spent on Website", "Page Views Per Visit"]  # [53] [120]
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train[num_var] = scaler.fit_transform(X_train[num_var])                   # [121]
    # test matrix scaled with the TRAIN scaler (correct practice; not what the notebook did)
    X_test_train_scaled = X_test.copy()
    X_test_train_scaled[num_var] = scaler.transform(X_test[num_var])
    # [193] the notebook RE-FITS the scaler on the test set: X_test[num_var] = scaler.fit_transform(...)
    X_test = X_test.copy()
    X_test[num_var] = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X_test[num_var])
    notes.append("Notebook re-fits StandardScaler on the test set ([193] scaler.fit_transform(X_test)); "
                 "X_test reproduces that. No numeric column is among the final features, so it does "
                 "not affect the final model's test predictions. X_test_train_scaled uses the "
                 "train-fitted scaler instead.")

    # ---- Step 5: RFE with LogisticRegression() defaults, 15 features             [124] [125]
    assert list(X_train.columns) == list(RFE_RANKING_REPORTED)                  # same design columns, same order
    assert sorted(RFE_SELECTED_REPORTED) == sorted(c for c, k in RFE_RANKING_REPORTED.items() if k == 1)
    rfe = run_rfe(X_train, y_train, RFE_RANKING_REPORTED, 15, notes)

    # ---- final model (logm4) on the notebook's final features                    [145]
    model = fit_mle(X_train[FINAL_FEATURES], y_train)
    coef = dict(zip(["const"] + FINAL_FEATURES, [model.intercept_[0]] + list(model.coef_[0])))
    max_coef_diff = max(abs(coef[k] - v) for k, v in COEF_REPORTED.items())
    print(f"final model: max |coef - notebook coef| = {max_coef_diff:.5f} (notebook prints 4 d.p.)")
    train_proba = model.predict_proba(X_train[FINAL_FEATURES].astype(float).values)[:, 1]
    test_proba = model.predict_proba(X_test[FINAL_FEATURES].astype(float).values)[:, 1]
    test_proba_ts = model.predict_proba(X_test_train_scaled[FINAL_FEATURES].astype(float).values)[:, 1]

    reproduced = {"train": metrics_at(y_train, train_proba, CUTOFF),
                  "test": metrics_at(y_test, test_proba, CUTOFF),
                  "extra": {"train_at_0.2": metrics_at(y_train, train_proba, 0.2),
                            "test_with_train_fitted_scaler": metrics_at(y_test, test_proba_ts, CUTOFF),
                            "max_abs_coef_diff_vs_notebook": max_coef_diff,
                            "coefficients": coef, "rfe": rfe}}
    print("TRAIN (cut-off %.2f):" % CUTOFF)
    show(REPORTED["train"], reproduced["train"])
    print("TEST  (cut-off %.2f):" % CUTOFF)
    show(REPORTED["test"], reproduced["test"])

    design_cols = list(X_train.columns)
    leaky_in_design = [s for s in LEAKY_SOURCES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for c in design_cols)]
    leaky_final = [c for c in FINAL_FEATURES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for s in LEAKY_SOURCES)]
    notes.append("Rows: 9,240 -> 9,074 after dropping rows with any missing value (Lead Source, "
                 "TotalVisits, Page Views Per Visit, Last Activity); split 70/30 random_state=100, "
                 "not stratified. Columns with >52% missing dropped (How did you hear, Lead Profile); "
                 "Lead Quality (51.59% missing) deliberately kept with NaN -> 'Not Sure'; Asymmetrique "
                 "x4 dropped by hand; Tags NaN -> mode 'Will revert after reading the email'. "
                 "TotalVisits and Page Views Per Visit capped at the 95th percentile of all 9,074 rows "
                 "before the split. Test cut-off 0.25 (precision-recall); train metrics are identical "
                 "at 0.2 (sensitivity-specificity choice).")
    out = {"name": NAME, "repo": REPO,
           "X_train": X_train, "X_test": X_test, "X_test_train_scaled": X_test_train_scaled,
           "y_train": y_train, "y_test": y_test,
           "train_index": np.asarray(X_train.index), "test_index": np.asarray(X_test.index),
           "final_features": FINAL_FEATURES, "cutoff": CUTOFF,
           "test_proba": test_proba, "train_proba": train_proba,
           "reported": REPORTED, "reproduced": reproduced,
           "leaky_final_features": leaky_final, "leaky_columns_in_design": leaky_in_design,
           "notes": " ".join(notes)}
    if out_path:
        with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(out, f)
    print("leaky final features:", leaky_final)
    print("leaky source columns in design matrix:", leaky_in_design)
    print("design matrix:", X_train.shape, X_test.shape, "->", out_path)
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: python ml/experiments/published/lsc.py <Leads.csv> [<out.pkl>]")
    reproduce(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)

"""Faithful re-implementation of Lead_Score_Case_Study, Lead_Case_Study_v1.ipynb.

usage: python ml/experiments/published/lscv1.py <path to Leads.csv> [<output .pkl path>]

Notebook cell numbers are given as [n] (0-based cell index of the .ipynb).
Only pandas / numpy / scikit-learn are used. The notebook's statsmodels GLM(Binomial) fit is
reproduced with an unpenalised sklearn LogisticRegression (same maximum-likelihood solution).
"""
import pickle
import sys
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.feature_selection import RFE
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, roc_auc_score
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

NAME = "lscv1"

                 "Asymmetrique Activity Index", "Asymmetrique Profile Index",
                 "Asymmetrique Activity Score", "Asymmetrique Profile Score"]

def metrics_at(y, p, cutoff):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    pred = (p > cutoff).astype(int)  # notebooks: 1 if x > cutoff else 0
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    n = len(y)
    return {"cutoff": float(cutoff), "n": int(n),
            "confusion": [[int(tn), int(fp)], [int(fn), int(tp)]],
            "accuracy": (tp + tn) / n, "sensitivity": tp / (tp + fn),
            "specificity": tn / (tn + fp), "precision": tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else float("nan"),
            "npv": tn / (tn + fn) if tn + fn else float("nan"), "fpr": fp / (tn + fp),
            "f1": 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), "roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, p))}


def run_rfe(X, y, reported_ranking, n_select, notes):
    """RFE(LogisticRegression(), n) as in the notebook, run two ways.

    The installed scikit-learn (1.6.1) minimises the MEAN log-loss with lbfgs and stops at
    gtol=tol, while the older versions the notebooks ran minimised C * SUM(log-loss) + penalty, so
    the same default tol=1e-4 stopped much later. LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / n_samples) reproduces the old stopping rule; the literal
    1.6.1 defaults are run as well and reported."""
    out = {}
    for key, est in (("old_sklearn_emulation", LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / len(X))),
                     ("sklearn_1_6_defaults", LogisticRegression())):
        r = RFE(est, n_features_to_select=n_select).fit(X, y)
        sel = list(X.columns[r.support_])
        rep_sel = [c for c in X.columns if reported_ranking[c] == 1]
        same = int(sum(reported_ranking[c] == k for c, k in zip(X.columns, r.ranking_)))
        out[key] = {"selected": sel, "selection_matches_notebook": set(sel) == set(rep_sel),
                    "identical_ranks": f"{same}/{X.shape[1]}",
                    "only_reproduced": sorted(set(sel) - set(rep_sel)),
                    "only_notebook": sorted(set(rep_sel) - set(sel))}
        print(f"RFE({n_select}) {key:22s}: selection == notebook: {set(sel) == set(rep_sel)}; "
              f"identical ranks {same}/{X.shape[1]}"
              + ("" if set(sel) == set(rep_sel) else
                 f"; only reproduced {out[key]['only_reproduced']}, only notebook {out[key]['only_notebook']}"))
    e, d = out["old_sklearn_emulation"], out["sklearn_1_6_defaults"]
    notes.append(f"RFE: old-sklearn emulation (tol=1e-4/n) matches the notebook's printed selection: "
                 f"{e['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks {e['identical_ranks']}); literal "
                 f"sklearn 1.6.1 defaults: {d['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks "
                 f"{d['identical_ranks']}, only reproduced {d['only_reproduced']}, only notebook "
                 f"{d['only_notebook']}). The final model uses the notebook's final feature list either way.")
    return out


def fit_mle(X, y):
    """Unpenalised logistic regression with intercept == statsmodels GLM(Binomial) MLE."""
    m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, solver="newton-cg", max_iter=10000, tol=1e-10)
    m.fit(X.astype(float).values, np.asarray(y))
    return m


def show(rep, rpr, keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity", "precision", "f1", "roc_auc")):
    for k in keys:
        a, b = rep.get(k), rpr.get(k)
        a_s = "   n/a  " if a is None else f"{a:.6f}"
        d = "" if a is None else f"  diff {100 * (b - a):+.3f} pp"
        print(f"    {k:12s} reported {a_s}  reproduced {b:.6f}{d}")
    print(f"    confusion    reported {rep.get('confusion')}  reproduced {rpr['confusion']}")

        X, y, train_size=0.7, test_size=0.3, random_state=100)                  # [122]

          f" precision {ts['precision']:.6f} auc {ts['roc_auc']:.6f} confusion {ts['confusion']}")

    design_cols = list(X_train.columns)
    leaky_in_design = [s for s in LEAKY_SOURCES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for c in design_cols)]
    leaky_final = [c for c in FINAL_FEATURES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for s in LEAKY_SOURCES)]
    notes.append(
        "Rows: 9,240 -> 9,103 (rows with missing TotalVisits/Page Views dropped) -> 8,953 after "

        "they are not in the design matrix. Split 70/30 random_state=100, not stratified. The "
        "notebook re-fits StandardScaler on the test set ([185]) and 'Total Time Spent on Website' "
        f"is a final feature; X_test reproduces that, X_test_train_scaled uses the train scaler "

        "train AUC 0.97 appears only in markdown.")
    out = {"name": NAME, "repo": REPO,
           "X_train": X_train, "X_test": X_test, "X_test_train_scaled": X_test_train_scaled,
           "y_train": y_train, "y_test": y_test,
           "train_index": np.asarray(X_train.index), "test_index": np.asarray(X_test.index),
           "final_features": FINAL_FEATURES, "cutoff": CUTOFF,
           "test_proba": test_proba, "train_proba": train_proba,
           "reported": REPORTED, "reproduced": reproduced,
           "leaky_final_features": leaky_final, "leaky_columns_in_design": leaky_in_design,
           "notes": " ".join(notes)}
    if out_path:
        with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(out, f)
    print("leaky final features:", leaky_final)
    print("leaky source columns in design matrix:", leaky_in_design)
    print("design matrix:", X_train.shape, X_test.shape, "->", out_path)
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: python ml/experiments/published/lscv1.py <Leads.csv> [<out.pkl>]")
    reproduce(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)

"""Faithful re-implementation of Lead-Scoring-Case-Study---Sivagiri,
"Lead Scoring Case Study -  Sivagiri.ipynb".

usage: python ml/experiments/published/sivagiri.py <path to Leads.csv> [<output .pkl path>]

Notebook cell numbers are given as [n] (0-based cell index of the .ipynb).
Only pandas / numpy / scikit-learn are used. The notebook's statsmodels GLM(Binomial) fit is
reproduced with an unpenalised sklearn LogisticRegression (same maximum-likelihood solution).
"""

NAME = "sivagiri"
REPO = "Lead-Scoring-Case-Study---Sivagiri (Lead Scoring Case Study -  Sivagiri.ipynb)"

                 "Asymmetrique Activity Index", "Asymmetrique Profile Index",
                 "Asymmetrique Activity Score", "Asymmetrique Profile Score"]

def metrics_at(y, p, cutoff):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    pred = (p > cutoff).astype(int)  # notebooks: 1 if x > cutoff else 0
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    n = len(y)
    return {"cutoff": float(cutoff), "n": int(n),
            "confusion": [[int(tn), int(fp)], [int(fn), int(tp)]],
            "accuracy": (tp + tn) / n, "sensitivity": tp / (tp + fn),
            "specificity": tn / (tn + fp), "precision": tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else float("nan"),
            "npv": tn / (tn + fn) if tn + fn else float("nan"), "fpr": fp / (tn + fp),
            "f1": 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), "roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, p))}


def run_rfe(X, y, reported_ranking, n_select, notes):
    """RFE(LogisticRegression(), n) as in the notebook, run two ways.

    The installed scikit-learn (1.6.1) minimises the MEAN log-loss with lbfgs and stops at
    gtol=tol, while the older versions the notebooks ran minimised C * SUM(log-loss) + penalty, so
    the same default tol=1e-4 stopped much later. LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / n_samples) reproduces the old stopping rule; the literal
    1.6.1 defaults are run as well and reported."""
    out = {}
    for key, est in (("old_sklearn_emulation", LogisticRegression(tol=1e-4 / len(X))),
                     ("sklearn_1_6_defaults", LogisticRegression())):
        r = RFE(est, n_features_to_select=n_select).fit(X, y)
        sel = list(X.columns[r.support_])
        rep_sel = [c for c in X.columns if reported_ranking[c] == 1]
        same = int(sum(reported_ranking[c] == k for c, k in zip(X.columns, r.ranking_)))
        out[key] = {"selected": sel, "selection_matches_notebook": set(sel) == set(rep_sel),
                    "identical_ranks": f"{same}/{X.shape[1]}",
                    "only_reproduced": sorted(set(sel) - set(rep_sel)),
                    "only_notebook": sorted(set(rep_sel) - set(sel))}
        print(f"RFE({n_select}) {key:22s}: selection == notebook: {set(sel) == set(rep_sel)}; "
              f"identical ranks {same}/{X.shape[1]}"
              + ("" if set(sel) == set(rep_sel) else
                 f"; only reproduced {out[key]['only_reproduced']}, only notebook {out[key]['only_notebook']}"))
    e, d = out["old_sklearn_emulation"], out["sklearn_1_6_defaults"]
    notes.append(f"RFE: old-sklearn emulation (tol=1e-4/n) matches the notebook's printed selection: "
                 f"{e['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks {e['identical_ranks']}); literal "
                 f"sklearn 1.6.1 defaults: {d['selection_matches_notebook']} (identical ranks "
                 f"{d['identical_ranks']}, only reproduced {d['only_reproduced']}, only notebook "
                 f"{d['only_notebook']}). The final model uses the notebook's final feature list either way.")
    return out


def fit_mle(X, y):
    """Unpenalised logistic regression with intercept == statsmodels GLM(Binomial) MLE."""
    m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, solver="newton-cg", max_iter=10000, tol=1e-10)
    m.fit(X.astype(float).values, np.asarray(y))
    return m


def show(rep, rpr, keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity", "precision", "f1", "roc_auc")):
    for k in keys:
        a, b = rep.get(k), rpr.get(k)
        a_s = "   n/a  " if a is None else f"{a:.6f}"
        d = "" if a is None else f"  diff {100 * (b - a):+.3f} pp"
        print(f"    {k:12s} reported {a_s}  reproduced {b:.6f}{d}")
    print(f"    confusion    reported {rep.get('confusion')}  reproduced {rpr['confusion']}")


def slots(x):                                                                   # [21]
    if x == "india":
        return "india"
    elif x == "not provided":
        return "not provided"
    return "outside india"


def reproduce(csv_path, out_path=None):
    """Re-run the notebook on csv_path; returns the dict described in published/__init__.py."""
    notes = []
    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)                                                  # [4]
    assert df.shape == (9240, 37)

    # ---- cleaning
    lower = lambda s: s.lower() if type(s) == str else s  # noqa: E731
    df = df.map(lower) if hasattr(pd.DataFrame, "map") else df.applymap(lower)  # [11] (applymap)
    df = df.replace("api", np.nan)                                              # [12] (comment says 'Select'!)
    nun = df.nunique()                                                          # [13]
    assert (nun["Lead Origin"], nun["Lead Source"], nun["Specialization"], nun["Tags"]) == (4, 20, 19, 26)
    df1 = df.drop(["Magazine", "Receive More Updates About Our Courses",
                   "I agree to pay the amount through cheque", "Get updates on DM Content",
                   "Update me on Supply Chain Content"], axis=1)                # [14]
    df2 = df1.drop(["Asymmetrique Profile Index", "Asymmetrique Activity Index",
                    "Asymmetrique Activity Score", "Asymmetrique Profile Score", "Lead Profile",
                    "Tags", "Lead Quality", "How did you hear about X Education", "City",
                    "Lead Number"], axis=1)                                     # [16]
    for c in ["Specialization", "What matters most to you in choosing a course", "Country",
              "What is your current occupation"]:
        df2[c] = df2[c].fillna("not provided")                                  # [18]
    df2["Country"] = df2.apply(lambda x: slots(x["Country"]), axis=1)           # [21]
    assert df2["Country"].value_counts().to_dict() == {"india": 6492, "not provided": 2461,
                                                       "outside india": 287}
    df3 = df2[df2.isnull().sum(axis=1) < 1]                                     # [24]
    assert len(df3) == 5496 and round(100 * df3.shape[0] / df.shape[0], 2) == 59.48  # [25] [28]
    df_final = df3.drop("Prospect ID", axis=1)                                  # [28]

    # ---- dummies                                                                  [49] [50]
    dummy = pd.get_dummies(df_final[["Lead Origin", "Specialization", "Lead Source", "Do Not Email",
                                     "Last Activity", "What is your current occupation",
                                     "A free copy of Mastering The Interview",
                                     "Last Notable Activity"]], drop_first=True).astype("uint8")
    df_final_dum = pd.concat([df_final, dummy], axis=1)
    assert df_final_dum.shape == (5496, 97)
    df_final_dum = df_final_dum.drop([
        "What is your current occupation_not provided", "Lead Origin", "Lead Source", "Do Not Email",
        "Do Not Call", "Last Activity", "Country", "Specialization", "Specialization_not provided",
        "What is your current occupation", "What matters most to you in choosing a course", "Search",
        "Newspaper Article", "X Education Forums", "Newspaper", "Digital Advertisement",
        "Through Recommendations", "A free copy of Mastering The Interview",
        "Last Notable Activity"], axis=1)
    assert df_final_dum.shape == (5496, 78)

    X = df_final_dum.drop(["Converted"], axis=1)                                # [52]
    y = df_final_dum["Converted"]                                               # [53]
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, train_size=0.7, test_size=0.3, random_state=10)                   # [54]
    assert list(X_train.index[:5]) == SPLIT_HEAD["train"]                       # [55] head
    assert list(X_test.index[:5]) == SPLIT_HEAD["test"]                         # [102] head
    assert X_train.shape == (3847, 77) and X_test.shape == (1649, 77)

    num = ["TotalVisits", "Page Views Per Visit", "Total Time Spent on Website"]
    scaler = MinMaxScaler()
    X_train[num] = scaler.fit_transform(X_train[num])                           # [55]
    X_test = X_test.copy()
    X_test[num] = scaler.transform(X_test[num])                                 # [100] train-fitted scaler
    X_test_train_scaled = X_test.copy()   # identical here: the notebook used the train scaler
    assert abs(X_train.loc[7700, "TotalVisits"] - 0.015936) < 5e-7              # [55] head
    assert abs(X_test.loc[5279, "Total Time Spent on Website"] - 0.087601) < 5e-7  # [102] head

    # ---- RFE with LogisticRegression() defaults, 15 features                   [59] [60]
    assert list(X_train.columns) == list(RFE_RANKING_REPORTED)
    rfe = run_rfe(X_train, y_train, RFE_RANKING_REPORTED, 15, notes)

    # ---- final model logm3                                                      [71]
    model = fit_mle(X_train[FINAL_FEATURES], y_train)
    coef = dict(zip(["const"] + FINAL_FEATURES, [model.intercept_[0]] + list(model.coef_[0])))
    max_coef_diff = max(abs(coef[k] - v) for k, v in COEF_REPORTED.items())
    print(f"final model: max |coef - notebook coef| = {max_coef_diff:.5f} (notebook prints 4 d.p.)")
    train_proba = model.predict_proba(X_train[FINAL_FEATURES].astype(float).values)[:, 1]
    test_proba = model.predict_proba(X_test[FINAL_FEATURES].astype(float).values)[:, 1]

    reproduced = {"train": metrics_at(y_train, train_proba, CUTOFF),
                  "test": metrics_at(y_test, test_proba, CUTOFF),
                  "extra": {"train_at_0.5": metrics_at(y_train, train_proba, 0.5),
                            "train_at_0.41": metrics_at(y_train, train_proba, CUTOFF_ALT),
                            "test_at_0.41": metrics_at(y_test, test_proba, CUTOFF_ALT),
                            "max_abs_coef_diff_vs_notebook": max_coef_diff,
                            "coefficients": coef, "rfe": rfe}}
    print("TRAIN (cut-off %.2f):" % CUTOFF)
    show(REPORTED["train"], reproduced["train"])
    print("TEST  (cut-off %.2f):" % CUTOFF)
    show(REPORTED["test"], reproduced["test"])
    print("TEST  (alternative cut-off %.2f, precision-recall):" % CUTOFF_ALT)
    show(REPORTED["extra"]["test_at_0.41"], reproduced["extra"]["test_at_0.41"],
         keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "precision"))
    print("TRAIN (cut-off 0.5) / (0.41):")
    show(REPORTED["extra"]["train_at_0.5"], reproduced["extra"]["train_at_0.5"],
         keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity", "precision"))
    show(REPORTED["extra"]["train_at_0.41"], reproduced["extra"]["train_at_0.41"],
         keys=("accuracy", "sensitivity", "precision"))

    design_cols = list(X_train.columns)
    leaky_in_design = [s for s in LEAKY_SOURCES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for c in design_cols)]
    leaky_final = [c for c in FINAL_FEATURES if any(c == s or c.startswith(s + "_") for s in LEAKY_SOURCES)]
    notes.append(
        "All string values are lower-cased first ([11]); then the notebook replaces 'api' (not "
        "'select') with NaN ([12], the comment says 'Select'), so every API-origin lead becomes "
        "missing and is removed by the complete-case filter ([24]): only 5,496 of 9,240 leads "
        "(59.48%, all non-API) are modelled, test n=1,649. 'select' is kept as a category "
        "(Specialization_select is a final feature). Tags, Lead Quality, Lead Profile and the "
        "Asymmetrique columns are dropped by hand ([16]) but Last Activity / Last Notable Activity "
        "are kept as dummies. Split 70/30 random_state=10, not stratified; MinMaxScaler fitted on "
        "train only and applied to test (no test re-fit), so X_test_train_scaled == X_test. "
        "Primary cut-off 0.35 (sensitivity/specificity, named in the summary PDF); the notebook "
        "also evaluates 0.41 (precision/recall) on test, kept under extra. No AUC is printed as text.")
    out = {"name": NAME, "repo": REPO,
           "X_train": X_train, "X_test": X_test, "X_test_train_scaled": X_test_train_scaled,
           "y_train": y_train, "y_test": y_test,
           "train_index": np.asarray(X_train.index), "test_index": np.asarray(X_test.index),
           "final_features": FINAL_FEATURES, "cutoff": CUTOFF, "cutoff_alt": CUTOFF_ALT,
           "test_proba": test_proba, "train_proba": train_proba,
           "reported": REPORTED, "reproduced": reproduced,
           "leaky_final_features": leaky_final, "leaky_columns_in_design": leaky_in_design,
           "notes": " ".join(notes)}
    if out_path:
        with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(out, f)
    print("leaky final features:", leaky_final)
    print("leaky source columns in design matrix:", leaky_in_design)
    print("design matrix:", X_train.shape, X_test.shape, "->", out_path)
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: python ml/experiments/published/sivagiri.py <Leads.csv> [<out.pkl>]")
    reproduce(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)

"""
Faithful re-implementations of four public solutions of the X Education lead-scoring case study
(the same Leads.csv, byte for byte), used by ml/experiments/published_benchmark.py to compare our
method with them on THEIR OWN train/test split and inputs.

Each module re-implements one notebook step by step (cell numbers in the comments) with pandas,
numpy and scikit-learn only (the notebooks' statsmodels GLM is the same maximum-likelihood fit as an
unpenalised LogisticRegression), checks itself against what the notebook printed (row counts, the
first rows of the split, scaled values, coefficients, the first predicted probabilities), and
reproduces every printed confusion matrix exactly.

    reproduce(csv_path) -> dict with X_train / X_test (the full design matrix the notebook's feature
    selection could choose from), X_test_train_scaled (the test rows scaled with the scaler fitted on
    the training rows), y_train / y_test, train_index / test_index (row numbers in Leads.csv),

    reproduced metrics, leaky_final_features, leaky_columns_in_design, notes.

# A/B engine check (simulated tests with known truth)

4,000 simulated tests per row, seed 2026.

| Check | Result | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| A/A tests (no real difference, 2 variants + control): engine declares a difference | 3.7% | at most 5% |
| 95% interval contains the true lift (+3 pts on 10%) | 95.2% | about 95% |
| Real +5 pt lift found with the planned 686 people per arm | 79.8% | about 80% |
| Split check false alarms (hash split, 3,000 people) | 0.0% | about 0.1% |
| Split check catches 10% of the control group lost (60 of 600 people) | 7.6% | low at this size: the check is strict (p < 0.001) |
| Split check catches 30% of the control group lost | 100.0% | high |

## End to end (analyse() on 4,000 simulated people, true lift of B = +6 pts)

- Day 5: **running** — Collecting outcomes: day 5 of 14
- Day 15: **winner** — Variant B wins: +6.2 points purchases vs sending nothing. 95% interval +3.2 points to +8.9 points, adjusted p = 0.0000.

| Arm | People | Bought | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | 767 | 57 | 7.4% |

## Adopted winners: the 10% check group (adoption.evaluate(), 200 simulated adoptions per row)

The old email sells to 10% of people; the adopted one truly sells 4 points more, the same, or 4 points less. The check confirms (95% interval above zero), switches back (interval below zero) or keeps checking.

| People who got the email since adoption | Truth | Confirmed | Still checking | Switched back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | adopted email better | 6% | 94% | 0% |
| 400 | adopted email no difference | 3% | 92% | 5% |
| 400 | adopted email worse | 0% | 78% | 22% |
| 1,500 | adopted email better | 26% | 74% | 0% |
| 1,500 | adopted email no difference | 2% | 91% | 7% |
| 1,500 | adopted email worse | 0% | 64% | 36% |
| 5,000 | adopted email better | 72% | 28% | 0% |
| 5,000 | adopted email no difference | 2% | 94% | 3% |
| 5,000 | adopted email worse | 0% | 8% | 92% |

With no real difference it should confirm or switch back about 2.5% of the time each (200 runs per row is noisy; the same statistics from counts, 20,000 runs each: wrongly confirmed 1.2%, 1.8%, 2.0%; wrongly switched back 3.5%, 3.1%, 2.5% for 400, 1,500, 5,000 people). A real 4-point difference needs a few thousand people before the 10% check group can show it; until then the dashboard says "collecting evidence".

# E8 The anchored update inside the product (simulated histories)

Each history is the CRM running by itself for 180 days on 2,000 simulated learners, with one setting changed. An extra 10% of learners (the evaluation group) is never contacted and never used for training: every retraining method's score is judged on their outcomes. At each monthly learning date the methods refit the lead score's live layer on the same logged decision points (the evaluation group left out). Made by `ml/experiments/anchored_histories.py` and `ml/experiments/anchored_check.py`.

What is judged: each score as "the chance to buy within 14 days if the CRM never contacts the lead", the same target as the learning loop's own control-group check. The comparison is offline: every method is fitted on the same logs, made by one run of the CRM (which retrained with the research kit's estimator during the history); how each method would change the CRM's later decisions is not measured here.

*Log-loss* is a proper scoring rule (lower is better; differences x1000, paired on the same rows, 95% interval from resampling people, each person's rows at every learning date kept together). *Over-states* = mean predicted chance to buy within 14 days over the share that bought, minus 1. *Targeted* = decision points where the CRM would have taken a step (where its own effect is largest).

## 5% control group, 15% random steps (v7.0's settings)

3 histories, 15 learning dates; at the last date on average 8,064 logged decision points to learn from and 166 evaluation-group learners.

# E7: capacity-aware next-best-action

10 simulated runs of 60 days (the first 7 build the price), 20 calls a day. Value is the true expected extra profit per day (INR) against doing nothing; 'share' is the part of the value of the call slots that each rule captures, between using no calls (0%) and the best allocation with hindsight (100%), with a 95% interval across runs.

Rules compared:

- **no calls**: calls are never used (what the other steps earn on their own)
- **first come**: the model's best step for each learner, a call while slots are left (the usual daily cap)
- **fixed price**: a call only when it adds more than one price, the same all day (from the last 7 days)
- **re-solved price**: ours: the price is worked out again at every decision from the slots left and the share of the day's call-worthy decisions still to come
- **hindsight**: the day's largest predicted call advantages (needs the day's future: the best any online rule could do with the same predictions)
- **true hindsight**: the same with the true advantages (the ceiling, with perfect prediction too)

## Summary

| Scenario | First come | Fixed price | Re-solved price (ours) | Ours against first come, INR per day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| demand 0.5x capacity | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | +0 (+/- 0) |
| demand 1x capacity | 93.7% | 93.8% | 97.0% | +1,915 (+/- 415) |
| demand 2x capacity | 70.3% | 89.8% | 95.5% | +23,258 (+/- 1,231) |
| demand 4x capacity | 52.3% | 89.3% | 96.2% | +55,286 (+/- 2,694) |
| demand 8x capacity | 40.7% | 88.7% | 96.8% | +88,039 (+/- 2,605) |
| demand 2x capacity, doubling half-way | 58.1% | 88.4% | 94.8% | +40,164 (+/- 1,674) |
| demand 4x capacity, doubling half-way | 45.5% | 88.5% | 96.5% | +72,984 (+/- 4,481) |

When demand for calls is 2x to 8x the capacity, first come, first served captures 41% to 70% of the value of the call slots; the re-solved slot price captures 96% to 97%, that is +23,258 to +88,039 INR a day with 20 calls a day. With spare capacity (0.5x) every rule uses the same calls, so pricing costs nothing when it is not needed.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| no calls | 61,871 | 0.0 | 0.0% (+/- 0.0) | -29,787 (+/- 857) |
| first come | 91,659 | 9.2 | 100.0% (+/- 0.1) | +0 (+/- 0) |
| fixed price | 91,659 | 9.2 | 100.0% (+/- 0.1) | +0 (+/- 0) |
| re-solved price | 91,659 | 9.2 | 100.0% (+/- 0.1) | +0 (+/- 0) |

# E8b What the random learning steps cost, and what next-best-action loses without them

Closed loop for 12 months, 1,000 new leads a month, in the worlds of E2b. The CRM starts from the model it ships with (trained on the documented assumptions) and retrains monthly exactly as the learning loop does (documented prior plus logged decisions, swap only on a clear off-policy gain). Same leads, true effects and random numbers for every share of random steps. Extra profit per lead over doing nothing, with the world's true effects (higher is better), as the mean of 5 independent runs per world (new leads and random numbers in each); swaps are the mean number of model replacements per run. Made by `ml/experiments/exploration_check.py`.

| World | Oracle | 0% random: what it did | 5% random: what it did | 15% random: what it did | 0%: learned policy, last month | 5%: learned policy, last month | 15%: learned policy, last month | Swaps (0% / 5% / 15%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
