# Where the learning loop's remaining gap comes from (simulated histories)

3 histories per rule (seeds 11, 12, 2026; 2,000 learners, 180 days; campaigns and A/B tests off), the same people and the same random draws under both rules. Each learning run checks the models on the untouched control group: how many of them each model expected to buy within 14 days, and how many did. Overstatement = expected / bought − 1, pooled over the runs of a history (weighted by the control group's decision points).

## 1. Later follow-ups in the outcome window

| Rule | History | Learning runs | CRM decisions | Control group bought (last run) | Naive expects | Ours expects | Naive overstates | Ours overstates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Usual | seed 11 | 6 | 4,607 | 23.4% (197 points) | 33.2% | 26.1% | +51.9% | +15.9% |
| Usual | seed 12 | 6 | 4,473 | 32.6% (193 points) | 34.8% | 29.0% | +2.7% | -15.0% |
| Usual | seed 2026 | 6 | 4,528 | 15.2% (211 points) | 37.5% | 28.4% | +156.9% | +106.7% |
| One touch per 14 days | seed 11 | 6 | 2,388 | 14.1% (99 points) | 22.6% | 19.5% | +54.9% | +34.0% |
| One touch per 14 days | seed 12 | 6 | 2,378 | 19.0% (105 points) | 23.9% | 18.8% | +35.8% | +6.9% |
| One touch per 14 days | seed 2026 | 6 | 2,337 | 14.8% (108 points) | 22.9% | 17.6% | +42.5% | +12.5% |

| Rule | Learning runs | Naive overstates | Ours overstates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Usual: the CRM decides at every trigger | 18 | +56.2% | +24.5% |
| One touch per 14 days: nothing else in a decision's outcome window | 18 | +43.8% | +16.9% |

Without later follow-ups in the outcome window, our model's gap goes from +24.5% to +16.9% (so later follow-ups explain part of it); the naive retrain's from +56.2% to +43.8%. Ours is below the naive retrain in every history. Single histories vary a lot (ours -15% to +107%): the control group is small.

## 2. Where the gap is: by the lead's age at the decision (last learning run of each history)

Two groups of people the CRM did nothing for at that moment: the **control group** (never worked on) and **worked-on leads it left alone by a random pick** (the 15% random choices). Pooled over the histories.

| Rule | Group | Younger than 7 days: points · bought · ours expects | 7 days or older: points · bought · ours expects |
|---|---|---|---|
| Usual | Control group (never worked on) | 344 · 22.4% · 19.7% (-12%) | 257 · 24.9% · 38.7% (+56%) |
| Usual | Worked-on leads, left alone by a random pick | 265 · 24.5% · 19.6% (-20%) | 160 · 28.1% · 33.0% (+17%) |
| One touch per 14 days | Control group (never worked on) | 228 · 13.2% · 13.0% (-1%) | 84 · 23.8% · 33.8% (+42%) |
| One touch per 14 days | Worked-on leads, left alone by a random pick | 147 · 11.6% · 11.4% (-1%) | 62 · 16.1% · 31.0% (+92%) |

Read with care: these are a few hundred decision points per cell (the control group is 5% of the learners); the pattern across the cells is the result, not the exact percentages.

## 3. The fix, tested here and used by the CRM: the lead's age as a learned input

The same live layer with the lead's age since sign-up (7–14 days, 14–30 days, 30+ days) as inputs that stay in the score, like time away. Out-of-fold, every history and both rules pooled:

| Group | Points | Bought | Ours expects (log-loss) | With lead age (log-loss) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Control group, younger than 7 days | 572 | 18.7% | 17.0% (-9%; 0.3241) | 19.6% (+5%; 0.3142) |
| Control group, 7 days or older | 341 | 24.6% | 37.5% (+52%; 0.5000) | 30.8% (+25%; 0.4414) |
| Control group, all | 913 | 20.9% | 24.7% (+18%; 0.3898) | 23.8% (+14%; 0.3617) |
| Worked-on leads, left alone by a random pick, younger than 7 days | 412 | 19.9% | 16.7% (-16%; 0.3629) | 19.4% (-3%; 0.3517) |
| Worked-on leads, left alone by a random pick, 7 days or older | 222 | 24.8% | 32.4% (+31%; 0.4788) | 27.2% (+10%; 0.4645) |
| Worked-on leads, left alone by a random pick, all | 634 | 21.6% | 22.2% (+3%; 0.4035) | 22.1% (+2%; 0.3912) |

Learned effect of the lead's age (log-odds, range over the histories): 7–14 days -1.18 to -0.35; 14–30 days -1.37 to -0.85; 30+ days -1.95 to -1.34.

# Next-best-action on a real randomized experiment (Hillstrom, 64,000 customers)

Arms: none 21,306, mens 21,307, womens 21,387. Randomization check: max |standardised mean difference| = 0.014.

| Arm | Visit rate | Conversion rate | Spend / customer |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 10.62% | 0.57% | $0.653 |
| mens | 18.28% | 1.25% | $1.423 |
| womens | 15.14% | 0.88% | $1.077 |

Cross-fitted: 5 folds × 3 repeats; models trained for **visit**.

## Q1 — Who to contact: ranking quality per email vs no email

Normalised Qini coefficient (0 = random, 1 = perfect) and uplift in visit rate (percentage points) among the top-ranked customers; mean ± sd over 15 held-out folds.

### Mens email vs no email

| Method | Qini coefficient | Uplift top 10% | Uplift top 20% | Uplift top 30% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Response model (GBM) | 0.023 ± 0.013 | +10.70 ± 3.11 | +9.52 ± 1.78 | +9.06 ± 1.18 |

# The simulated histories, checked against what is known to be true

6 histories (different random seeds), each 180 days, 2,000 simulated learners, the CRM running by itself: scoring, next-best-action with 15% random learning steps, campaigns with hold-outs, six A/B tests, auto-adopted winners, and the learning loop at days 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 and the end. The untouched control group is 5% of learners (never contacted). Made by `ml/experiments/history_check.py` from the history databases.

- **Ours is each step's effect from the CRM's own experiment against its never-contacted control group (v7.1; the control group also gives those effects, and each person is predicted by a model fitted without them; ml/results/anchored_check.md judges on a group nothing learns from).** Against v7.0's retrain (told what the CRM did, effects learned by the model), on the control group: better in **10**, worse in **7** and the same in 19 of 36 runs (the same: no step had enough control-group decision points yet, so the update works as v7.0's); mean log-loss ours 0.4108, v7.0 0.4144, naive 0.4588. Over-statement of the control group's buying, mean over these runs: ours +44%, v7.0 +50%, naive +80%.

- Runs with a control-group check: **36**. Ours predicted the control group better (lower log-loss) than the naive retrain in **31 of 36**, and better than the model in use at that time in 23 of 36.
- The usual check (fit on all live outcomes, which the CRM's own follow-ups shaped) would have picked the naive retrain in **35 of 36** runs.
- How much each overstated the control group's buying, mean over all runs: naive **+80%**, ours **+44%**, the model in use before the run +62%. (Ours' remaining gap sits in leads older than a week: ml/results/followups_check.md; the loop also learns the lead's age: ml/results/lead_age_check.md.)
- Final runs only (most data): naive +59%, ours +23%.
- Lead model swapped 7 times over 36 runs (only when better on the control group in ≥90% of bootstrap resamples); next-best-action swapped 2 times.

## 2. What the loop learned about this business, vs the truth

The simulated business differs from the base model's training data in three documented ways (log-odds of buying, `WORLD_DRIFT` in backend/app/simulation/behaviour.py). Below: what the final learning run of each history learned (ours), and whether the CRM is using a learned model.

| History | Opted in to WhatsApp (true +0.6) | Browses on mobile (true -0.5) | Joined a webinar (true +0.7) | Largest other corrections | Model in use at the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| seed 2026 | +0.62 | -0.41 | +0.62 | Clicked our emails -0.71, Downloaded a brochure +0.50, Added to cart +0.32 | learned model from 2026-10-25 |
| seed 11 | +0.54 | -0.26 | +0.48 | Clicked our emails -0.62, Watched a course video +0.27, Read testimonials +0.20 | learned model from 2026-09-25 |
| seed 12 | +0.77 | -0.45 | +0.39 | Clicked our emails -1.56, Started checkout +0.43, Added to cart +0.19 | learned model from 2026-10-25 |
| seed 13 | +0.60 | -0.57 | +0.38 | Clicked our emails -1.02, Opened chat +0.27, Added to cart +0.19 | learned model from 2026-09-25 |
| seed 14 | +0.52 | -0.37 | +0.52 | Clicked our emails -0.73, Downloaded a brochure +0.16, Watched a course video +0.16 | learned model from 2026-07-27 |
| seed 15 | +0.51 | -0.45 | +0.34 | Clicked our emails -1.14, Started checkout +0.47, Sent an enquiry +0.35 | learned model from 2026-07-27 |

Learned vs true, range over the histories: Opted in to WhatsApp +0.51 to +0.77 (true +0.6, right sign in 6 of 6); Browses on mobile -0.57 to -0.26 (true -0.5, right sign in 6 of 6); Joined a webinar +0.34 to +0.62 (true +0.7, right sign in 6 of 6).

Weights are log-odds added for a lead with the signal. They are ridge-shrunk toward 0 and fitted together with a recalibration of the base score, so only the sign and rough size should match.
The large negative correction for *Clicked our emails* is not one of the designed differences, and it is right: in the base model's training data email opens depend only on the learner's interest, but in a running CRM they also depend on how many emails the CRM has already sent (learners it kept emailing without a purchase pile up clicks), so a click says less about interest than the base model assumed.
A learned model is used only once the untouched control group confirms it with 90% confidence. With about 80 untouched people after six months that bar is high: where no model was confirmed, the CRM kept the starting model even though the new one was often better (section 1). A larger control group or a lower bar (crm_settings.json) makes it switch sooner, at the cost of fewer people worked on or more risk of switching on noise.

The naive retrain learns similar signal weights to ours (median difference 0.04, largest 0.50 log-odds). Its main mistake is the overall level: most decision points were followed by an action of the CRM, and the naive retrain folds the average effect of those actions into every lead's baseline — which is what section 1 shows.

## 3. The CRM's total impact (worked-on leads vs the untouched control group)

Share of learners who bought within 30 days of signing up (learners who signed up at least 30 days before the end).

| History | Worked on | Control group | Difference (95% interval) | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seed 2026 | 449/1524 = 29.5% | 8/78 = 10.3% | +19.2 pts (+10.2 to +24.7) | 0.000 |
| seed 11 | 497/1562 = 31.8% | 13/80 = 16.2% | +15.6 pts (+5.7 to +22.5) | 0.003 |
| seed 12 | 495/1533 = 32.3% | 20/80 = 25.0% | +7.3 pts (-3.4 to +15.8) | 0.173 |
| seed 13 | 467/1561 = 29.9% | 19/80 = 23.8% | +6.2 pts (-4.5 to +14.5) | 0.239 |
| seed 14 | 501/1531 = 32.7% | 15/78 = 19.2% | +13.5 pts (+3.1 to +21.1) | 0.013 |
| seed 15 | 458/1532 = 29.9% | 13/78 = 16.7% | +13.2 pts (+3.2 to +20.3) | 0.012 |

Mean difference +12.5 pts, positive in 6 of 6 histories; the 95% interval is above zero in 4 of 6 (the control group is only ~5% of learners, so each single history has a wide interval).
All 6 independent histories together: worked on 2,867/9,243 = 31.0%, control group 88/474 = 18.6%: **+12.5 pts** (95% interval +8.6 to +15.8, p = 0.0000).

## 5. The pipeline in rupees, inside the product

Each learner's first automatic decision with a full 14-day outcome window before the end of the history, in 6 histories. The control group is chosen at random and never contacted, so the difference between worked-on leads and the control group is what the CRM's work added. *Expected* is what the CRM's numbers said at that moment (the score in use then); *actual* is the revenue (fee paid, after any discount) within the window, per learner, with a 95% interval from resampling learners. The worked-on leads' actual revenue includes every later step of the CRM within the window, while the estimate counts only the first step.

**All first decisions** (10,056 learners, 477 of them in the control group)

| | Expected per learner | Actual per learner (95% interval) |
|---|---|---|
| Control group: comes in anyway (chance to buy with no step x fee) | ₹7,903 | ₹6,459 (₹4,889 to ₹8,099) |
| Worked-on leads: with the step the CRM took | ₹9,783 | ₹9,639 (₹9,222 to ₹10,061) |
| What the CRM's work adds: the step it took (its own estimate) against worked-on minus control | ₹2,310 | ₹3,180 (₹1,511 to ₹4,800) |
| The best step's extra profit (what the pipeline calls 'the team can add') | ₹2,627 | |

Share who bought within the window: control group 13.8% against an expected 16.6%; worked-on leads 21.2% against 22.8%.

# E6 Learned lead aging vs hand-set decay rules (simulated histories)

3 new histories (seeds 11, 12, 2026; 2,000 learners, 180 days; campaigns and A/B tests on, as in the product), made by the CRM's own code with lead aging switched on. Judged at the last learning run on people the CRM did nothing for at that moment, out-of-fold. Log-loss is a proper scoring rule (lower = better ranking AND more honest probabilities); calibration error by lead age = weighted mean |expected − actual| over the age groups (<7, 7–14, 14–30, 30+ days). Intervals: 95%, cluster bootstrap over people.

# E3 Learning loop on real randomized data (Hillstrom, 42,613 customers: men's email vs none)

50 repeats (random splits: 10% before the CRM, two rounds of 30%, 30% held out). The CRM emails the top 30% by its score, 15% of its choices random, and never contacts its 5% control group; it retrains twice. Everything is judged on held-out customers the real experiment left alone (visit rate 10.6%). Intervals: 95%, corrected resampled t-test (Nadeau & Bengio 2003).

## The precise metric: feedback bias

**Feedback bias** = mean predicted minus actual visit rate of held-out customers the randomized experiment left alone (percentage points). A score that learned the CRM's own emails as customer quality over-predicts what customers do when nobody contacts them. No selection is involved, so the no-loop reference sits at zero.

| Method | Feedback bias (points) | In % of the true rate | Over-predicts its own targeted 30% by | Honest AUC | Honest log-loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Naive retrain (how CRMs retrain) | +2.35 [+1.80, +2.89] | +22 [+16, +28]% | +37.7 [+28.0, +47.4]% | 0.637 | 0.3294 |
| Control group only (clinical-ML holdout approach) | +0.08 [-0.92, +1.08] | +1 [-9, +10]% | +19.2 [+3.0, +35.4]% | 0.614 | 0.3322 |
| Left-alone customers, weighted (IPW) | +0.04 [-0.83, +0.92] | +0 [-8, +9]% | +16.3 [+0.8, +31.7]% | 0.622 | 0.3311 |
| **Ours** (told what the CRM did) | +0.33 [-0.31, +0.96] | +3 [-3, +9]% | +9.3 [+1.3, +17.3]% | 0.638 | 0.3257 |
| Reference: no loop at all (oracle) | +0.05 [-0.54, +0.64] | +1 [-5, +6]% | +6.7 [-1.5, +14.9]% | 0.637 | 0.3256 |

- **Best of all deployable methods on one proper scoring rule:** ours has the lowest honest log-loss of naive, holdout, IPW and ours in **49 of 50** repeats (and is level with the no-loop oracle: lower in 20 of 50).
- **Ours removes 88 [72, 104]% of the feedback bias** of naive retraining; ours minus the no-loop reference: +0.28 [-0.09, +0.65] points. Ours is less biased than naive in **50 of 50** repeats.
- Against the clinical-ML holdout approach (unbiased by construction, but it learns from the control group only): honest AUC +0.024 [+0.010, +0.037] higher, log-loss +0.0065 [+0.0023, +0.0106] lower with ours (ours better in 50 and 50 of 50).
- Against IPW (left-alone customers, weighted): the same idea, but the weights (up to 13x) make it noisy: its feedback bias varies with sd 0.65 points between repeats, ours 0.47.
- Against naive: honest AUC +0.001 [-0.007, +0.009], log-loss +0.0037 [+0.0017, +0.0057] lower with ours (ours more accurate on the truth in 49 of 50).
- The last column includes the winner's curse: picking the top 30% of any noisy score over-predicts them (the no-loop reference: +6.7%); scores learned from fewer people are noisier, so the holdout and IPW models show more of it.

## The accuracy illusion

| Method | AUC on the data its own policy logged | Honest AUC | Illusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Naive retrain (how CRMs retrain) | 0.683 | 0.637 | +0.046 [+0.036, +0.056] |
| Control group only (clinical-ML holdout approach) | 0.660 | 0.614 | +0.046 [+0.035, +0.057] |
| Left-alone customers, weighted (IPW) | 0.667 | 0.622 | +0.045 [+0.035, +0.055] |
| **Ours** (told what the CRM did) | 0.681 | 0.638 | +0.043 [+0.033, +0.053] |
| Reference: no loop at all (oracle) | 0.681 | 0.637 | +0.044 [+0.033, +0.055] |

Every model looks better on the data its own emails shaped: an AUC measured on a CRM's own logged data is not its accuracy.

## Choosing the model: naive vs ours

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Truth: honest log-loss on all held-out left-alone customers | ours better in 49 of 50 |
| Usual check: log-loss on the CRM's own logged data | picks naive in **50 of 50** |
| Our check with naive in place: the control group, swap if better in >= 90% of 300 resamples | swaps to ours in 11 of 50; otherwise keeps naive |
| Our check with ours in place | swaps to naive in **2 of 50** |

The held-out period's control group has 323 left-alone people on average: our check rarely makes a wrong swap; with so few people it often keeps the current model (the right swap needs more control-group outcomes).

## Different exploration rates

| Random share of the CRM's choices | Feedback bias, naive (points) | Feedback bias, ours | Bias removed | Honest AUC naive / ours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0% (25 repeats) | +2.24 [+1.62, +2.86] | +0.30 [-0.49, +1.09] | 90 [72, 107]% | 0.636 / 0.639 |
| 5% (25 repeats) | +2.24 [+1.62, +2.86] | +0.32 [-0.42, +1.07] | 89 [72, 106]% | 0.637 / 0.639 |
| 15% (50 repeats) | +2.35 [+1.80, +2.89] | +0.33 [-0.31, +0.96] | 88 [72, 104]% | 0.637 / 0.638 |
| 30% (25 repeats) | +2.48 [+1.91, +3.05] | +0.37 [-0.33, +1.06] | 88 [76, 100]% | 0.638 / 0.637 |

Ours needs customers the CRM did NOT email among those it would target (overlap). The random choices give some, and so does the control group, which the CRM never contacts: that is why the result hardly depends on the exploration rate here, even at 0%.

# Our lead-scoring method on real data (9,240 real X Education leads, 9 leak-free columns)

5-fold cross-validation x 3 seeds (mean ± sd). Lower log-loss / Brier / calibration error is better.

| Model | AUC | Log-loss | Brier | Calibration error | Bought among the top 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boosting + neural network, averaged | 0.875 ± 0.000 | 0.4258 ± 0.0005 | 0.1354 | 0.013 | 94.9% |
| Gradient boosting | 0.874 ± 0.001 | 0.4265 ± 0.0009 | 0.1357 | 0.009 | 94.5% |
| Random forest | 0.875 ± 0.001 | 0.4314 ± 0.0006 | 0.1367 | 0.040 | 94.8% |
| Neural network, 2 hidden layers (64-32) | 0.868 ± 0.001 | 0.4369 ± 0.0024 | 0.1394 | 0.019 | 94.5% |
| Neural network, 3 hidden layers (128-64-32) | 0.867 ± 0.002 | 0.4379 ± 0.0025 | 0.1400 | 0.015 | 94.2% |
| Neural network, calibrated | 0.868 ± 0.000 | 0.4436 ± 0.0009 | 0.1393 | 0.013 | 94.3% |
| Logistic regression | 0.838 ± 0.000 | 0.4798 ± 0.0001 | 0.1558 | 0.037 | 91.7% |

TabPFN was not installed here, so it is not in the table (pip install tabpfn to add it).

For contrast — gradient boosting WITH the post-contact columns (Tags, Lead Quality, Last Notable Activity, Last Activity, Lead Profile): AUC 0.980, accuracy 94.2%. Those columns are written by sales after contacting the lead, so a new lead never has them: that number cannot be reached in real use.

The CRM's own base model (trained only on simulated leads) applied to these real leads as they are: AUC 0.612, average predicted chance 7.6% vs 38.5% who actually bought. The real file has none of the website signals (video, pricing, cart, checkout ...) the model mostly relies on, so it cannot be judged on this file. In the running CRM every lead has those signals, and the learning loop corrects the base model from the CRM's own outcomes, checked on the untouched control group.

# E9: the money features against known truth

Simulated learners whose true response to every step is known, the production code and the starting models (lead_model.starter.pkl, nba_model.starter.pkl). Every rule sees the same learners in the same order with the same predictions and is scored with the true probabilities as expected profit (no outcome noise). INR throughout.

## a. A monthly discount budget

10 runs of 2 months (300 automatic decisions a weekday, fewer at weekends; the first 7 days only build the price). If every coupon that pays were sent, a month of coupons would cost about 10,059,890 of expected discount; the budgets below are shares of that. Calls are left out here (E7 prices them). 'Share' is the part of the value of the budget that each rule captures, between no coupons (0%) and the best allocation with hindsight (100%), with a 95% interval across months and runs. 'Budget used' is the true expected discount given, as a share of the budget (the rules count the predicted cost when a coupon goes out, as the CRM does for open coupons).

Rules compared:

- **no coupons**: no coupon is ever given (what the other steps earn on their own)
- **cart recovery**: the usual rule: a 10% coupon to every left cart while money is left; everyone else gets the model's best step without a coupon
- **first come**: the model's best step for each learner, coupons included, until the money is used up
- **fixed price**: a coupon only when it adds more than one price per rupee of discount, the same all month (from the week before the month)
- **re-solved price**: ours (production app.ml.budget): the price is worked out again at every decision from the money left, the days left and the last 7 days of decisions
- **hindsight**: the best single price for the month, chosen knowing the whole month's decisions in advance (the best any rule could do with the same predictions)
- **true hindsight**: the same with the true effects and costs (the ceiling, with perfect prediction too)

| Budget | First come | Cart recovery | Fixed price | Re-solved price (ours) | Ours against first come, a month |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10% (1,005,989) | 37.3% | -26.3% | 95.3% | 96.8% | +1,573,914 (+/- 38,217) |
| 25% (2,514,973) | 49.9% | -35.5% | 89.2% | 99.8% | +2,482,130 (+/- 57,589) |
| 50% (5,029,945) | 61.6% | -43.4% | 93.5% | 99.2% | +3,057,503 (+/- 80,169) |
| 100% (10,059,890) | 98.5% | -38.4% | 98.8% | 99.8% | +136,908 (+/- 76,839) |

## b. The coupon guard

Coupons a counsellor might give by hand. The guard stops a coupon when its predicted extra profit (chance to buy with it x fee x (1 - discount) - chance without it x fee) is not positive. 'Precision': of the stopped coupons, the share that truly lose money; 'recall': of the coupons that truly lose money, the share stopped. Profit is per 100 coupons the counsellor wanted to give.

| Coupons for | Discount | Stopped | Truly lose money | Precision | Recall | Profit, all given | Profit, guard on | Saved | Discount to buyers anyway avoided |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the warmest leads (top 10% by score) | 10% | 100% | 98% | 98% | 100% | -383,894 | 0 | 383,894 | 438,065 |
| the warmest leads (top 10% by score) | 20% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | -801,491 | 0 | 801,491 | 876,130 |
| every left cart | 10% | 59% | 61% | 96% | 93% | -48,034 | 158,673 | 206,707 | 242,870 |
| every left cart | 20% | 67% | 67% | 95% | 95% | -258,336 | 178,177 | 436,513 | 538,142 |
| anyone (10% at random) | 10% | 36% | 35% | 74% | 76% | 98,852 | 156,172 | 57,320 | 91,878 |
| anyone (10% at random) | 20% | 45% | 42% | 80% | 86% | 67,230 | 211,164 | 143,934 | 227,424 |

## c. The pipeline in rupees

200 snapshots of 1,200 open leads. 'Comes in anyway' is the sum of each lead's chance to buy with no contact x fee; 'the team can add' is the sum of the best step's extra profit.

| | Predicted | True | Predicted / true |
|---|---|---|---|
| Comes in anyway | 18,985,429 | 18,958,782 | 1.001 |
| The team can add (best step for every lead) | 4,743,635 | 4,666,279 | 1.017 |

By fifths of the lead score:

| Lead score | Anyway, predicted / true | Can add per lead, predicted | Can add per lead, true |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.004 to 0.069 | 0.925 | 1,787 | 1,635 |
| 0.069 to 0.154 | 1.018 | 3,444 | 3,296 |
| 0.154 to 0.320 | 0.998 | 4,948 | 4,923 |
| 0.320 to 0.650 | 0.998 | 6,319 | 6,244 |
| 0.650 to 1.000 | 1.007 | 3,239 | 3,329 |

When the team has time for only some of the open leads, each worked with the model's best step: the true profit added when they are worked in the usual order (highest score first), in money order (most to add first, the pipeline's default), at random, and with perfect knowledge (the ceiling).

| Leads worked | Highest score first | Most to add first (ours) | Random | Perfect knowledge | Ours against highest score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 (5%) | 40,316 (4%) | 874,900 (89%) | 229,510 (24%) | 978,420 | +834,583 (+/- 7,418) |
| 120 (10%) | 193,262 (12%) | 1,415,563 (89%) | 462,883 (29%) | 1,588,622 | +1,222,300 (+/- 9,896) |
| 240 (20%) | 797,639 (32%) | 2,271,329 (91%) | 930,284 (37%) | 2,501,642 | +1,473,691 (+/- 12,903) |
| 480 (40%) | 2,299,796 (62%) | 3,451,426 (93%) | 1,863,147 (50%) | 3,710,557 | +1,151,630 (+/- 12,094) |

'No discount needed' (more likely than not to buy anyway, and no coupon would add profit by the model: 20.4% of the leads who can get email): for 91% of them even the better coupon truly loses money (on average 2,859 a lead). Being likely to buy anyway is not enough on its own: for all such leads (28.2%) the share is 73%; for every other lead it is 15%.

## d. The owner's planner

What one more counsellor (8 more call slots a day on top of 8) would add in a month: the planner's estimate (from the last 7 days of predicted call advantages, production app.services.planner.slots_value) against the true extra profit of the same days run with the extra slots (re-solved slot price, E7). The planner replays last week's decisions with the CRM's own rule; 'ranked' is the simpler estimate it does not use (each day's calls ranked 9 to 16 by predicted advantage), which misses that with more slots the rule holds back fewer calls for later in the day. Demand is the number of call-worthy decisions a day as a multiple of today's slots.

| Demand | Today's slots: estimate | true | estimate / true | One more counsellor: estimate | true | estimate / true | ranked / true |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1x | 547,794 | 542,470 | 1.01 (+/- 0.04) | 57,401 | 61,509 | 0.89 (+/- 0.13) | 0.31 |
| 2x | 919,464 | 899,190 | 1.02 (+/- 0.03) | 193,546 | 204,809 | 0.95 (+/- 0.05) | 0.81 |
| 4x | 1,401,105 | 1,389,185 | 1.01 (+/- 0.03) | 570,275 | 558,237 | 1.02 (+/- 0.04) | 1.02 |
| 8x | 1,883,119 | 1,818,069 | 1.04 (+/- 0.02) | 999,139 | 968,427 | 1.03 (+/- 0.02) | 1.05 |

# Next-best-action robustness: worlds where our assumptions are wrong

**20 random worlds.** Beat the best fixed policy (chosen in hindsight): ours 20/20, flexible 20/20, champion/challenger 20/20. Median share of oracle profit: ours 83.1% (worst 55.6%), flexible 81.5% (worst 60.7%), champion/challenger 86.8% (worst 60.0%), best fixed 27.4%. The interpretable model beat the flexible one in 9/10 worlds with hidden share < 0.5 and 4/10 with hidden share ≥ 0.5 (correlation of hidden share with the interpretable model's advantage: -0.70). The champion/challenger rule picked the better family in 13/20.

# What-if paths: out-of-time check

6 histories: in each, the paths are learned from the decisions before a cut-off (two thirds into the history) and tested on the later decisions, weighted by 1/probability.

| History | Learned from / tested on | same mix for everyone | mix per stage (ignores the step) | what-if paths (stage and step) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seed2026 | 2,762 / 2,051 | 0.5576 | 0.5449 | 0.5465 |
| seed11 | 2,867 / 1,935 | 0.5630 | 0.5415 | 0.5289 |
| seed12 | 2,688 / 2,086 | 0.5638 | 0.5402 | 0.5467 |
| seed13 | 2,708 / 2,073 | 0.5877 | 0.5792 | 0.5719 |
| seed14 | 2,845 / 2,161 | 0.5476 | 0.5264 | 0.5245 |
| seed15 | 2,612 / 2,094 | 0.5470 | 0.5361 | 0.5260 |
| Mean | | 0.5611 | 0.5447 | 0.5407 |

Brier score of the reaction in the next 3 days (lower is better). The what-if paths beat the mix per stage in 4 of 6 histories (mean difference -0.0040).

| Team step | Later decisions | Predicted buying within 14 days | Actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Counsellor phone call | 2,066 | 28.3% | 34.3% |
| Send email with 10% coupon | 1,524 | 34.6% | 37.7% |
| Send email with 20% coupon | 3,517 | 37.1% | 38.3% |
| Send an information email | 2,588 | 33.8% | 33.3% |
| Do nothing for now | 1,995 | 28.8% | 32.7% |
| WhatsApp message | 710 | 37.9% | 42.3% |
| All steps | 12,400 | 33.1% | 35.6% |

# E1b Our lead scoring vs published solutions (X Education, 9,240 real leads)

Same data (byte-identical Leads.csv), same rows, same inputs. The precise metric is ROC AUC on the identical test rows with DeLong's 95% interval and paired test, repeated on 30 new splits with the corrected resampled t-interval; accuracy is compared at a cut-off chosen on the training rows by each solution's own rule (McNemar's exact test).

**Post-contact columns** (Tags, Lead Quality, Lead Profile, Last Activity, Last Notable Activity, Asymmetrique scores) are filled in by the sales team after contacting a lead, so a new lead never has them: a model that uses them cannot score new leads.

## The records, in one table

| Comparison | Best earlier result (published, or their model re-run) | Ours | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same rows and same inputs as each of 4 public solutions | AUC 0.864–0.972 | higher by +0.004 to +0.030 on their split; better in 30 of 30 new splits for each (every 95% interval above zero) | DeLong on the identical test rows; 30 new 70/30 splits |
| Only inputs a new lead has | AUC 0.8605 (Mandal 2025, stratified 80/20); 0.864 (Lohani & Bansal, on its split) | AUC 0.874 on 50 stratified 80/20 splits (above 0.8605 in 98%); 0.875 on Lohani & Bansal's split — with 9 columns | their protocol |
| With post-contact columns (not valid for new leads) | AUC 0.972, accuracy 93.0% | AUC 0.984 [0.982, 0.987], accuracy 94.7% | 5-fold cross-validation |

## A. Four public solutions, re-run exactly, on their own splits

## B. Published results whose code is not public

| Publication | Post-contact columns | Their protocol | Their result | Ours |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| [Jadli et al., Indian J. Computer Science and Engineering 13(2), 2022](https://doi.org/10.21817/indjcse/2022/v13i2/221302098) | not stated | 9,074 rows x 89 columns after preprocessing | random forest: accuracy 93.0%, AUC 0.92 | with post-contact columns (5-fold CV): AUC 0.984, accuracy 94.7%. Without them the best accuracy in this study is 81.4%: above 90% needs post-contact columns |
| [Yim et al., Int. J. Management, Finance and Accounting 5(1), 2024](https://doi.org/10.33093/ijomfa.2024.5.1.2) | not stated in the abstract | 10-fold cross-validation | stacking: accuracy 92.3% | with post-contact columns (5-fold CV): AUC 0.984, accuracy 94.7%. Without them the best accuracy in this study is 81.4%: above 90% needs post-contact columns |

## What this shows (computed from the numbers above)

- **Same rows, same inputs:** on each solution's own split our AUC is higher for all 4 (3 significantly, DeLong p < 0.05; 1 not significantly; 0 lower), and on 30 new splits ours is better in 30, 30, 30, 30 of 30 with every interval above zero. Nothing was tuned on their data: the gradient boosting is the CRM's own configuration.
- **Their high numbers come from post-contact columns.** Refitted without those columns, each solution's own model falls: shinde-chandrakant AUC 0.939 → 0.599; Sivagiri12 AUC 0.882 → 0.862; ShahadShaikh AUC 0.972 → 0.785.
- **On what a new lead has**, our 9-column model scores AUC 0.871–0.886 on the four splits; against the only leak-free public solution (Lohani & Bansal) on its own rows: +0.011 [+0.004, +0.017] (DeLong p 0.0009), and +0.013 [+0.009, +0.016] over 30 new splits (better in 30). Under the leak-free thesis's protocol it reaches AUC 0.874 on average (98% of 50 splits above the thesis's 0.8605).
- **The honest ceiling.** Without post-contact columns no model in this study goes beyond AUC 0.886 or accuracy 81.4%. The accuracies above 90% reported for this file (two of the public solutions, which use post-contact columns; Jadli et al.; Yim et al., whose inputs are not listed) are out of reach for a model that scores new leads.
- Leads in the file: 9,240; converted 38.5%.

"""
Writes docs/API.md (every route, grouped as in the interactive documentation) and docs/openapi.json from the
backend's own OpenAPI description, so the reference always matches the code.

    backend/.venv/bin/python scripts/api_reference.py          (Windows: backend\\.venv\\Scripts\\python ...)
    ... scripts/api_reference.py --check                       fail if docs/ is out of date (used by CI)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "backend"))

INTRO = """# API reference

Generated from the backend's OpenAPI description by `scripts/api_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. The running
backend serves the same reference interactively at http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/docs (try any request there) and the
machine-readable description at `/api/openapi.json` (also saved as [openapi.json](openapi.json)).

## Conventions

- Two APIs share one server. `/api/v1/...` is the learner website's API, `/api/v1/crm/...` the CRM team's API.
- Sign-in returns a JSON Web Token; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Learner and team tokens have
  different audiences, so neither opens the other API. A token stops working when its account's password changes.
- Team roles are checked on every request: **admin** (everything), **marketing** (campaigns, A/B tests, coupons,
  exports, the learning loop) and **counsellor** (leads, today's actions, callbacks, pipeline, questions; changes
  only their own leads and unassigned ones). Reading campaigns and tests is open to the whole team.
- Errors are JSON: `{"detail": "a sentence a person can act on"}` with the usual status codes (400 invalid input,
  401 not signed in, 403 not allowed for this role, 404 not found, 409 conflict, 422 malformed request,
  429 too many attempts, 503 a dependency such as email is unavailable).
- Every response carries `X-Request-ID` (sent back when the caller supplies one) and the security headers
  `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Times are the server's local time as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`; money is in Indian rupees.
"""


def build() -> tuple[str, str]:
    from app.main import app

    spec = app.openapi()
    groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
    order: list[str] = []
    for path, methods in spec["paths"].items():
        for method, op in methods.items():
            tag = (op.get("tags") or ["Other"])[0]
            if tag not in order:
                order.append(tag)
            groups[tag].append((method.upper(), path, op.get("summary", "")))
    lines = [INTRO.rstrip(), ""]
    total = sum(len(v) for v in groups.values())
    lines += [f"{total} routes in {len(order)} groups.", ""]
    for tag in order:
        lines += [f"## {tag}", "", "| Method | Path | What it does |", "|---|---|---|"]
        for method, path, summary in groups[tag]:
            lines.append(f"| {method} | `{path}` | {summary} |")
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines), json.dumps(spec, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="fail when docs/API.md or docs/openapi.json is out of date")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    md, spec = build()
    targets = {ROOT / "docs" / "API.md": md, ROOT / "docs" / "openapi.json": spec}
    if args.check:
        stale = [p.name for p, text in targets.items() if not p.exists() or p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != text]
        if stale:
            print(f"Out of date: {', '.join(stale)}. Run python scripts/api_reference.py")
            return 1
        print("The API reference is up to date.")
        return 0
    for path, text in targets.items():
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"Wrote {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""
Fails when an emoji appears in the project's own files: code, settings, styles, pages and documents.

    python scripts/check_no_emoji.py              check the whole project
    python scripts/check_no_emoji.py PATH ...     check these files or folders

Typographic characters are not emoji and stay allowed: the rupee sign, the minus and multiplication signs, dashes and
arrows in comments and formulas. Generated or third-party folders (node_modules, dist, data, caches) are skipped.
Exit code 0 when clean, 1 when an emoji was found (each one is listed with its file, line and code point).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SKIP_DIRS = {
    ".git",
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    "coverage",
    "__pycache__",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "data",
}
SUFFIXES = {
    ".py", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".mjs", ".css", ".html", ".json", ".md", ".txt", ".toml", ".ini", ".cfg",
    ".yml", ".yaml", ".bat", ".cmd", ".ps1", ".sh", ".mako", ".svg",
}  # fmt: skip
EMOJI = re.compile(
    "["
    "\U0001f000-\U0001faff"  # pictographs, emoticons, transport, flags, playing cards, chess and more
    "\u2600-\u27bf"  # miscellaneous symbols and dingbats (sun, telephone, check marks, stars)
    "\u2b00-\u2bff"  # symbols and arrows drawn as emoji (stars, circles, squares)
    "\u2300-\u23ff"  # technical symbols drawn as emoji (watch, hourglass, keyboard)
    "\ufe0f"  # emoji presentation selector
    "\u200d"  # zero-width joiner (joins emoji into one)
    "\u20e3"  # keycap
    "]"
)
ALLOWED = {"\u2318", "\u2325", "\u2303", "\u23ce"}  # keyboard keys shown in shortcut hints


def files(paths: list[Path]):
    for path in paths:
        if path.is_file():
            yield path
            continue
        for p in sorted(path.rglob("*")):
            parts = set(p.relative_to(path).parts)
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in SUFFIXES and not SKIP_DIRS & parts and p.name != "package-lock.json":
                yield p


def scan(paths: list[Path]) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    for path in files(paths):
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
            for match in EMOJI.finditer(line):
                if match.group() in ALLOWED:
                    continue
                shown = path.relative_to(ROOT) if path.is_relative_to(ROOT) else path
                problems.append(f"{shown}:{number}: U+{ord(match.group()):04X}")
    return problems


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    targets = [Path(a).resolve() for a in argv] or [ROOT]
    problems = scan(targets)
    for p in problems:
        print(p)
    if problems:
        print(f"{len(problems)} emoji found. Use words instead.")
        return 1
    print("No emoji found.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""
Measures how fast the real-time loop answers on a running backend: a website event until the learner's new score
comes back (POST /api/v1/track, timed in this script and inside the server), over many events of one test learner.
The learner uses the reserved .test domain (never emailed) and is deleted at the end with everything linked to it.

    backend/.venv/bin/python scripts/latency_check.py [--events 300] [--api URL] [--db PATH] [--email ADMIN]

The CRM password (for the server-side timings on the Learning loop page) is asked for, or read from CRM_PASSWORD.
Prints the median, the 95th percentile and the maximum, in milliseconds.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import getpass
import os
import random
import statistics
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from smoke_test import ROOT, Client, code_from_inbox  # noqa: E402

EVENTS = ["page_view", "page_view", "page_view", "video_play", "pricing_view", "brochure_dl", "testimonial_view"]


def quantile(values: list[float], q: float) -> float:
    ordered = sorted(values)
    return ordered[min(len(ordered) - 1, int(q * len(ordered)))]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--api", default=os.getenv("API_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000"))
    ap.add_argument("--email", default=os.getenv("CRM_OWNER_EMAIL", "admin@xeducation.in"))
    ap.add_argument("--events", type=int, default=300)
    default_db = Path(os.getenv("DATA_DIR") or ROOT / "backend" / "data") / "xeducation.db"
    ap.add_argument("--db", type=Path, default=default_db)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    api = Client(args.api)
    password = os.getenv("CRM_PASSWORD") or getpass.getpass(f"CRM password of {args.email}: ")
    code, r = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/crm/auth/login", {"email": args.email, "password": password})
    if code != 200:
        print("Could not sign in to the CRM with that email address and password.")
        return 1
    crm = r["token"]

    email = f"latency.{int(time.time())}@checks.xeducation.test"
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/auth/signup", {"name": "Latency Check", "email": email, "password": "Latency-2026"})
    _, r = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/auth/verify-otp", {"email": email, "otp": code_from_inbox(args.db, email)})
    learner = r["token"]
    _, courses = api.call("GET", "/api/v1/courses")
    slugs = [c["slug"] for c in courses["courses"]]
    _, s = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/session/start", {"device_type": "Desktop"}, token=learner)

    rng = random.Random(7)
    timings = []
    print(f"\nSending {args.events} website events ...")
    for _ in range(args.events):
        body = {
            "session_id": s["session_id"],
            "course_slug": rng.choice(slugs),
            "event_type": rng.choice(EVENTS),
            "time_spent_sec": rng.randint(5, 240),
        }
        started = time.perf_counter()
        code, _ = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/track", body, token=learner, quiet=True)
        if code == 200:
            timings.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
    _, server = api.call("GET", "/api/v1/crm/latency", token=crm)
    api.call("DELETE", "/api/v1/me", token=learner)

    if not timings:
        print("No event was answered.")
        return 1
    print(f"\nEvent to new score, {len(timings)} events, over HTTP on this computer:")
    print(
        f"  median {statistics.median(timings):.0f} ms, 95th percentile {quantile(timings, 0.95):.0f} ms, "
        f"max {max(timings):.0f} ms"
    )
    inside = (server or {}).get("event_to_score")
    if inside:
        print(
            f"Inside the server (scoring only, last {inside['count']} events of any learner): "
            f"median {inside['median_ms']:.0f} ms, 95th percentile {inside['p95_ms']:.0f} ms"
        )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def call(api: str, method: str, path: str, body=None, token: str | None = None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        api + path,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
        method=method,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **({"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"} if token else {})},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode() or "{}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read().decode()[:300]


def copy_data(dst: Path) -> Path:
    src = BACKEND / "data"
    shutil.copytree(src, dst, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("xeducation.db*", "logs", "initial-admin-password.txt"))
    with sqlite3.connect(src / "xeducation.db") as a, sqlite3.connect(dst / "xeducation.db") as b:
        a.backup(b)
    return dst / "xeducation.db"


def start_api(data: Path, port: int) -> subprocess.Popen:
    env = {**os.environ, "DATA_DIR": str(data), "SCHEDULER_ENABLED": "false", "SIMULATION_ENABLED": "false"}
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "app.cli", "serve", "--port", str(port)],
        cwd=BACKEND, env=env, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )  # fmt: skip
    for _ in range(240):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/ready", timeout=5) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return proc
        except OSError:
            pass
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            break
        time.sleep(0.5)
    proc.kill()
    raise SystemExit(f"The copy's API did not start on port {port}.")


def reading(api: str, email: str, password: str) -> dict:
    s, r = call(api, "POST", "/crm/auth/login", {"email": email, "password": password})
    if s != 200:
        raise SystemExit("Could not sign in to the CRM with that email address and password.")
    token = r["token"]
    out = {p: call(api, "GET", p, token=token) for p in READS}
    for q in QUESTIONS:
        s, r = call(api, "POST", "/crm/copilot", {"question": q}, token)
        out["Ask: " + q] = (s, {"answer": r.get("answer"), "data": (r.get("tools") or [{}])[0].get("data")})
    return out


def _plain(text: str) -> str:
    """An answer without its real/simulated breakdown ("(1 real person, 97 simulated)", "204 of these are ...")."""
    text = text.replace(NEW, SIM)
    text = re.sub(r" \([\d,]+ real (person|people), [\d,]+ simulated\)", "", text)
    return re.sub(r" [\d,]+ of these are simulated learners\.", "", text)


def walk(a, b, path: str, out: list) -> None:
    if isinstance(a, dict) and isinstance(b, dict):
        for k in sorted(set(a) | set(b)):
            if k not in SPLIT:
                walk(a.get(k), b.get(k), f"{path}.{k}", out)
    elif isinstance(a, list | tuple) and isinstance(b, list | tuple):
        if len(a) != len(b):
            out.append((path, f"{len(a)} items", f"{len(b)} items"))
        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)):
            walk(x, y, f"{path}[{i}]", out)
    elif isinstance(a, int | float) and isinstance(b, int | float) and not isinstance(a, bool):
        if not math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-9):  # the same number (up to float rounding)
            out.append((path, a, b))
    elif isinstance(a, str) and isinstance(b, str):
        if _plain(a) != _plain(b) and not a[:4].isdigit():  # dates and times are clocks
            out.append((path, a[:120], b[:120]))
    elif a != b:
        out.append((path, str(a)[:120], str(b)[:120]))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--email", default=os.getenv("CRM_OWNER_EMAIL", "admin@xeducation.in"))
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)
    ap.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    password = os.getenv("CRM_PASSWORD") or getpass.getpass(f"CRM password of {args.email}: ")
    api = f"http://127.0.0.1:{args.port}/api/v1"
    work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="real-vs-simulated-"))
    try:
        db = copy_data(work / "data")
        with sqlite3.connect(db) as con:
            n = con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE email LIKE ?", (f"%{SIM}",)).fetchone()[0]
        if not n:
            print("There are no simulated learners in this CRM, so there is nothing to compare.")
            return 0
        print(f"Copied the data to {work}; {n:,} simulated learners. Reading every page ...")
        proc = start_api(work / "data", args.port)
        try:
            before = reading(api, args.email, password)
        finally:
            proc.terminate()
            proc.wait(30)
        with sqlite3.connect(db) as con:
            con.execute("UPDATE users SET email = REPLACE(email, ?, ?) WHERE email LIKE ?", (SIM, NEW, f"%{SIM}"))
        print(f"Turned the {n:,} simulated learners into real people. Reading every page again ...")
        proc = start_api(work / "data", args.port)
        try:
            after = reading(api, args.email, password)
        finally:
            proc.terminate()
            proc.wait(30)
        if args.keep:
            (work / "before.json").write_text(json.dumps(before, default=str))
            (work / "after.json").write_text(json.dumps(after, default=str))
        failed, differences = [k for k, (s, _) in {**before, **after}.items() if s != 200], 0
        for k in before:
            out: list = []
            walk(before[k], after.get(k), "", out)
            differences += len(out)
            print(f"{'same' if not out else 'DIFFERENT'}  {k}")
            for path, x, y in out[:5]:
                print(f"      {path}: before {x!r}, after {y!r}")
        print(
            f"\n{len(before)} pages and answers compared: {differences} differences besides the real/simulated split"
            + (f"; not answered: {', '.join(sorted(set(failed)))}" if failed else "")
        )
        return 1 if differences or failed else 0
    finally:
        if not args.keep:
            shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""
Checks a running X Education backend end to end over HTTP, the way the website and the CRM use it: every CRM page's
data, a learner's whole journey (sign-up with the emailed code, profile, a visit, wishlist, cart, enquiry, chat,
callback, question, purchase, review), the team answering the callback and the question, and finally the learner
deleting their account. Prints one line per request and exits with 1 if any request failed.

    backend/.venv/bin/python scripts/smoke_test.py                   macOS, Linux
    backend\\.venv\\Scripts\\python scripts\\smoke_test.py             Windows

Options: --api URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8000), --email (a CRM admin; default CRM_OWNER_EMAIL or
admin@xeducation.in), --db PATH (the backend's database, to read the test learner's code from its inbox).
The CRM password is asked for (or read from the CRM_PASSWORD environment variable) and never printed.

The test learner uses the reserved .test domain: it is never emailed (its code waits in the database's
simulated_inbox table) and it is deleted at the end, with everything linked to it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import getpass
import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CRM_READS = [
    "/me",
    "/stats",
    "/stats/daily?days=30",
    "/forecast",
    "/priority-queue",
    "/model/health",
    "/nba/performance",
    "/campaign-influence",
    "/capacity",
    "/leads?limit=5",
    "/leads?tier=Customers&limit=5",
    "/leads?segment=real&limit=5",
    "/actions",
    "/callbacks",
    "/coupons",
    "/whatsapp/log",
    "/campaigns",
    "/ab-tests",
    "/ab-tests/plan",
    "/adoptions",
    "/learning/overview",
    "/latency",
    "/journeys",
    "/pipeline",
    "/pipeline?sort=score",
    "/money",
    "/planner",
    "/start",
    "/copilot",
    "/qna",
    "/team",
    "/team/performance",
    "/audit?limit=20",
    "/simulation",
]
QUESTIONS = [
    "How many leads came in this week?",
    "Who should we call today?",
    "Which leads are most likely to buy?",
    "What is a call slot worth today?",
    "Is the CRM actually making a difference?",
    "What is the pipeline worth?",
    "Should we hire another counsellor?",
]


class Client:
    def __init__(self, base: str):
        self.base = base.rstrip("/")
        self.failures: list[str] = []

    def call(self, method, path, body=None, token=None, expect=(200,), quiet=False):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else (b"" if method in ("POST", "PUT") else None)
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
                code, raw, kind = r.status, r.read().decode(), r.headers.get("content-type", "")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            code, raw, kind = e.code, e.read().decode(), e.headers.get("content-type", "")
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            sys.exit(f"The API at {self.base} does not answer ({e.reason}). Start it first (start-all).")
        out = json.loads(raw) if raw and kind.startswith("application/json") else raw
        ok = code in expect
        if not quiet or not ok:
            print(f"{'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {code} {method} {path.split('?')[0]}")
        if not ok:
            self.failures.append(f"{method} {path}: {code} {str(out)[:200]}")
        return code, out


def code_from_inbox(db_path: Path, email: str, attempts: int = 20) -> str:
    for _ in range(attempts):
        con = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        try:
            row = con.execute(
                "SELECT subject FROM simulated_inbox WHERE email=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1", (email,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            con.close()
        found = re.search(r"code: (\d{6})", row[0]) if row else None
        if found:
            return found.group(1)
        time.sleep(0.5)
    return "000000"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--api", default=os.getenv("API_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000"))
    ap.add_argument("--email", default=os.getenv("CRM_OWNER_EMAIL", "admin@xeducation.in"))
    default_db = Path(os.getenv("DATA_DIR") or ROOT / "backend" / "data") / "xeducation.db"
    ap.add_argument("--db", type=Path, default=default_db)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    api = Client(args.api)
    if api.call("GET", "/api/health")[0] != 200:
        return 1
    password = os.getenv("CRM_PASSWORD") or getpass.getpass(f"CRM password of {args.email}: ")

    code, r = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/crm/auth/login", {"email": args.email, "password": password})
    if code != 200:
        print("Could not sign in to the CRM with that email address and password.")
        return 1
    if r["member"].get("must_change_password"):
        print("This account still has its first password: sign in to the CRM once and choose your own.")
        return 1
    crm = r["token"]
    for path in CRM_READS:
        api.call("GET", "/api/v1/crm" + path, token=crm)
    for question in QUESTIONS:
        api.call("POST", "/api/v1/crm/copilot", {"question": question}, token=crm)

    # a learner's journey
    email = f"smoke.{int(time.time())}@checks.xeducation.test"
    password_l = f"Smoke-{int(time.time())}"
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/auth/signup", {"name": "Smoke Tester", "email": email, "password": password_l})
    code, r = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/auth/verify-otp", {"email": email, "otp": code_from_inbox(args.db, email)})
    if code != 200:
        print("The test learner could not be verified; is --db the backend's database?")
        return 1
    learner = r["token"]
    _, courses = api.call("GET", "/api/v1/courses")
    slug = courses["courses"][0]["slug"]
    api.call("GET", f"/api/v1/courses/{slug}")
    api.call("GET", "/api/v1/faq")
    api.call("GET", "/api/v1/profile/options")
    profile = {
        "current_occupation": "Working Professional",
        "specialization": "Finance Management",
        "city": "Pune",
        "phone": "+91 98765 43210",
    }
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/profile/complete", profile, token=learner)
    _, s = api.call("POST", "/api/v1/session/start", {"device_type": "Desktop", "lead_source": "Google"}, token=learner)
    for event, seconds in (("page_view", 120), ("pricing_view", 40), ("video_play", 200)):
        body = {"session_id": s["session_id"], "course_slug": slug, "event_type": event, "time_spent_sec": seconds}
        api.call("POST", "/api/v1/track", body, token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/session/ping", {"session_id": s["session_id"]}, token=learner)
    for path in ("/live-score", "/me/insights", "/recommendations", "/dashboard"):
        api.call("GET", "/api/v1" + path, token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/wishlist", {"course_slug": slug}, token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/cart", {"course_slug": slug}, token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/checkout/start", token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/coupons/check", {"code": "NOT-A-CODE"}, token=learner, expect=(400,))
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/enquiry", {"course_slug": slug, "phone": "+91 98765 43210"}, token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/chat", {"message": "What are the fees?", "course_slug": slug}, token=learner)
    callback = {"phone": "+91 98765 43210", "preferred_time": "Evening", "course_slug": slug}
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/callback", callback, token=learner)
    question = f"Is there a weekend batch? ({email})"
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/qna", {"course_slug": slug, "question": question}, token=learner)

    # the team sees them and answers
    _, found = api.call("GET", f"/api/v1/crm/leads?search={email}", token=crm)
    if found.get("leads"):
        lead_id = found["leads"][0]["id"]
        for part in ("", "/now", "/attribution", "/explain", "/paths"):
            api.call("GET", f"/api/v1/crm/leads/{lead_id}{part}", token=crm)
        # the coupon guard, and taking a step by hand (refused only for the control group)
        uid = found["leads"][0]["user_id"]
        api.call("GET", f"/api/v1/crm/coupons/check?user_id={uid}&discount_pct=10", token=crm)
        api.call("POST", f"/api/v1/crm/leads/{lead_id}/act", {"action": "email_info"}, token=crm, expect=(200, 409))
    _, callbacks = api.call("GET", "/api/v1/crm/callbacks", token=crm)
    for c in callbacks.get("callbacks", []):
        if c.get("email") == email:
            api.call("POST", f"/api/v1/crm/callbacks/{c['id']}/done", {"note": "Smoke test"}, token=crm)
    _, questions = api.call("GET", "/api/v1/crm/qna", token=crm)
    for q in questions.get("questions", []):
        if q.get("question") == question:
            api.call("POST", "/api/v1/crm/qna/answer", {"qna_id": q["id"], "answer": "Yes, on Saturdays."}, token=crm)

    # they buy, review, and delete their account
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/checkout", {"coupon_code": ""}, token=learner)
    api.call("GET", "/api/v1/purchases", token=learner)
    api.call("POST", "/api/v1/reviews", {"course_slug": slug, "rating": 5, "review_text": "Clear."}, token=learner)
    api.call("DELETE", "/api/v1/me", token=learner)
    api.call("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me", token=learner, expect=(401,))

    print(f"\n{len(api.failures)} failed request(s)" if api.failures else "\nEvery request answered as expected.")
    for f in api.failures:
        print("  " + f)
    return 1 if api.failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
